title: refactor: extract shared loadFixture helper from test files
description: R3-LOW-28. loadFixture function is duplicated in js/tests/graph/build-plan-graph.test.ts and build-resource-graph.test.ts with identical implementation: reads fixture file, parses with parsePlanJson, throws on failure. Fix: create js/tests/helpers/load-fixture.ts with the shared function and import from both test files. Flagged by: Code Quality (HIGH).

title: Refactor FlowCanvas state to useReducer
description:
Consolidate the 7 useState calls in flow-canvas.tsx into a single useReducer.

Current state: 7 independent useState calls (selectedNode, selectedNodeId, hoveredNodeId, filterDiffState, showLateralEdges, showPhantomLeaves, isolatedLateralNodeId) with coordinated multi-set patterns in handlePaneClick, handleClosePanel, and handleNodeClick.

What changes:
- Define CanvasState type and CanvasAction discriminated union
- Replace 7 useState with one useReducer
- selectedNode + selectedNodeId merge into one field (selectedNode carries id), eliminating the state duplication where DagNodeData omits the node id
- Scattered set* calls become named dispatches (CLEAR_SELECTION, SELECT_NODE, HOVER_NODE, SET_FILTER, TOGGLE_LATERAL_EDGES, TOGGLE_PHANTOM_LEAVES, ISOLATE_LATERAL)
- The ~15 useMemo derivations stay unchanged, just read from state.fieldName

What it doesn't change:
- File size stays roughly the same (reducer function adds ~30 lines, removes ~20 lines of useState/set*)
- useMemo derivation chain is untouched
- useCallback handlers still needed for referential stability, just become one-liner dispatches

Discovered during React Crusade audit (W3 state duplication + W4 useState count).

title: Lateral edges between synced tables and their source-table phantoms
description: Add lateral edges connecting synced_database_tables resources to their source-table phantom nodes. Currently synced tables and their source-table phantoms both appear in the UC tree but have no visual connection — they're linked only implicitly by sharing a schema parent. A lateral edge from the synced table resource node to its source-table:: phantom (derived from spec.source_table_full_name) would make the data lineage relationship explicit. These would be extracted in extractLateralEdges or a similar step, using the same source_table_full_name field that creates the phantom.

title: Lateral edge extraction: consistency and collision fixes
description:
Three related issues from review:

1. Missing nodeIds.has(sourceNodeId) guard in extractDatabaseInstanceEdges and extractServingEndpointModelEdges — inconsistent with extractWarehouseEdges which does the check. Low risk since nodeIdByResourceKey is built from allNodes, but should be consistent.

2. Lateral edge IDs use the same source→target format as hierarchy edges. If a lateral edge coincides with a depends_on or hierarchy edge, duplicate IDs would confuse React Flow. Prefix lateral IDs with 'lateral::' to guarantee uniqueness.

3. extractPipelineTargetEdges could emit duplicate edges for the same pipeline→schema pair if ingestion_definition.objects has redundant entries. Add a seen-set dedup within the function.

title: LateralDependencyEntry and PhantomContextEntry share fields
description: Both types share label, resourceKey, and resourceType fields. LateralDependencyEntry adds nodeId and diffState. Could extract a shared base type, but they serve different conceptual purposes so keeping separate is also defensible.

title: Clean up useNodeDimming exports and unused return fields
description: NodeDimmingResult type is exported but never imported outside use-node-dimming.ts. Several return fields (isDimmed, dimOpacity, isHovered, isSelected, isFilterHighlighted) are computed but never destructured by any caller. Unexport the type and consider removing or lazy-computing unused fields.

title: Surface drift between remote and old state in plan
description:
Detect when a job was manually edited outside the bundle (break glass) and warn in CLI output.

Detection rule: for each change entry, if old is defined AND new is defined AND old == new, but remote differs or is absent, that field was silently changed by the server. The most reliable signal is edit_mode flipping from UI_LOCKED to EDITABLE — this is a binary indicator that someone broke glass.

Scope: CLI text mode warning only. The browser visualization already shows the correct remote→new delta after the dagshund-j5zd fix. Adding drift hues to the graph creates combinatorial visual complexity (modified-with-drift? added-but-drifted?) and the edge coloring problem is unsolvable without a new color language. A CLI warning before the diff output is sufficient.

Example output:
  ⚠ drift detected: resources.jobs.drift_pipeline was manually edited
    edit_mode, tasks[task_key=publish].depends_on[0].task_key, tasks[task_key=transform]

Fixture: fixtures/drift-plan.json (captured from real Databricks deployment with manual edits).
close_reason: Implemented — CLI warns inline and in summary when resources were manually edited outside the bundle

title: Eliminate unnecessary type assertions in change-path.ts
description:
Two 'as' casts in change-path.ts can be eliminated:

1. Line 173: `arr[i] as Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>` after an `isPlainObject` guard — TypeScript loses narrowing because `arr[i]` is re-evaluated. Fix: bind `arr[i]` to a local variable before the guard.

2. Lines 231-233: `stateValue as Record<string, unknown>` after typeof+null+isArray guards. Fix: use the existing `isPlainObject` type guard instead of manual checks + cast.

Also consider extracting the duplicated `isPlainObject` helper (exists in both change-path.ts and structural-diff.ts) into a shared utility.

title: Add paneClickDistance={5} for consistency with nodeClickDistance
description: nodeClickDistance={5} was added to fix node click suppression from d3-drag. The same d3-zoom click suppression can affect pane clicks (onPaneClick clears selection). Add paneClickDistance={5} to ReactFlow for consistency. Lower priority since pane clicks are less frequent and less affected.

title: isUnknownRecord type guard does not exclude arrays
description: unknown-record.ts:11-12 — isUnknownRecord checks typeof value === 'object' && value \!== null but does not exclude arrays. An array would pass the guard and be cast to Record<string, unknown>. Not reachable from current data sources (Databricks plan state objects are always plain objects at the checked nesting levels), but defensively incorrect. Fix: add && \!Array.isArray(value) to the guard.

title: task: theming infrastructure — CSS variables, dark/light toggle, OS preference
description:
Foundation for the UI overhaul. Set up the theming system that everything else builds on. Part of epic dagshund-4y6.

## Deliverables
- CSS custom properties (design tokens) for colors, shadows, borders, radii — defined for both dark and light modes
- Databricks-inspired color palette: muted blues/grays, professional feel, dagshund identity
- Tailwind config extended with theme tokens where appropriate
- Dark/light mode toggle component (sun/moon icon button)
- OS preference detection via prefers-color-scheme media query
- Manual override persisted to localStorage
- Diff state colors (green/red/amber) tuned for readability in both modes
- Base body/background/text colors applied globally

title: weekly scheduled pipeline: dep-scan rerun + outdated tooling check
description:
Add a scheduled pipeline (cron: Sunday UTC) that:

- Re-runs `dependency-scan` (OSV-Scanner against uv.lock + js/bun.lock) to catch CVE disclosures landing against unchanged lockfiles between releases.
- Reports tooling versions that have newer releases available — analogous to Dependabot/Renovate but lightweight.

## Design options

- **Simple:** one job runs `uv pip list --outdated` + `bun outdated` and fails (or opens an issue via glab) if anything is behind.
- **Renovate Bot:** full MR automation. Heavier setup, more noise, handles the full loop including MR open.
- **Custom:** small script comparing pinned versions (UV_IMAGE, OSV_SCANNER_IMAGE digests, BUN_VERSION, ALPINE_IMAGE digest) against upstream release feeds, piped into a scheduled GitLab issue.

Start with the simple version — can upgrade to Renovate later if manual triage becomes annoying.

## Wiring

Top-level `workflow:` rules need a new case: `$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule"`. Schedule itself configured in GitLab UI (Settings → CI/CD → Schedules) with a Sunday cron. Jobs that should run under schedule get a matching rule.

## Context

Scoped out of the `dagshund-3hep` hardening MR because it needs a manual GitLab UI step (Schedule creation) and has an unmade design call that deserves its own review.

title: Fixture regeneration tooling for upstream CLI changes
description:
Local-only tooling for generating golden plan.json fixtures from real Databricks workspaces. Never runs in CI — no Databricks credentials are exposed outside the developer machine.

## Requirements

- Databricks CLI >= 0.295 with engine set to `direct` (per docs)
- Bundle schema generated from CLI (user provides this)
- Each fixture needs a deploy/plan/capture/destroy cycle against a real workspace

## Workflow per fixture

1. Deploy bundle A (databricks.yaml) to establish baseline state in workspace
2. Plan bundle B against that deployed state — this produces the diff JSON (the fixture)
3. Capture and sanitize the plan output (PII: emails, workspace paths, job IDs)
4. Destroy the deployed state so the workspace is clean for the next fixture

## Folder structure

Databricks CLI requires a file called `databricks.yaml` in the working directory — one per folder, no exceptions. Each golden fixture therefore needs its own folder containing the before and after bundle configs:

```
fixtures/golden/<name>/
  before/databricks.yaml   — bundle config for baseline (deployed first)
  after/databricks.yaml    — bundle config for changed state (planned against baseline)
  plan.json                — captured and sanitized plan output
  expected.txt             — expected CLI text output (optional, for regression)
```

The tooling orchestrates the cycle: cd into before/, deploy, cd into after/, plan with `-o json`, capture output, sanitize, place as plan.json, then destroy the deployed state.

## What the tooling does NOT do

- Run in CI (local-only, human-driven)
- Commit or push (human reviews sanitized output, then commits)
- Manage Databricks credentials (assumes CLI is already authenticated)

Part of epic dagshund-1mxn.

title: refactor: rename FORBIDDEN_RESPONSE factory to createForbiddenResponse
description: R3-LOW-25. FORBIDDEN_RESPONSE in index.ts:58 uses SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (suggesting a constant) but is actually a factory function () => new Response('Forbidden', {status:403}). Per naming conventions, functions should be camelCase verb-first. Fix: rename to createForbiddenResponse. Flagged by: Code Quality (MEDIUM).

title: Add test cases for chooseLateralHandles edge cases
description: chooseLateralHandles only has one indirect test case via toLateralFlowEdges (source above target). Add cases for: source below target, same Y position, and horizontal-dominant separation where all handle combos have equal dy.

title: extract NodeFrame + resolveDriftBorder to DRY resource/task/hierarchy nodes
description:
Resource/task/hierarchy node components share a copy-pasted shell.

Shared frame (resource-node.tsx:36-84, task-node.tsx:27-59, hierarchy-node.tsx:32-67):
- Outer div with identical class string: rounded-lg border-2 px-4 py-1.5 + styles.{border,background,text} + borderStyle + opacityClass + glowStyle
- Target Handle with visibility gated on hasIncoming
- Label span with diffBadge + truncated label + optional DriftPill
- Badge row (typeBadge / phantom badge / LateralIsolateButton)
- Source Handle with visibility gated on hasOutgoing
- Optional LateralHandles

Drift-border computation is literally identical in resource + task:
  const isDrift = data.nodeKind === 'X' && data.isDrift === true
  const borderStyle = isDrift ? 'border-dashed' : styles.borderStyle

Hierarchy variant is the same shape but with isPhantom instead of isDrift.

## Won't-fix (2026-04-17)

Attempted the refactor; surface duplication is shallow while the semantic divergences are real. A unified NodeFrame ends up as a variant switcher, not a shell:

- Resource has job navigation, type badges, drift detection, lateral edges
- Task has none of the above — no lateral edges, no job nav
- Hierarchy has phantoms (not drift), font-semibold outer, different label structure (no flex, no DriftPill, font-normal override on badge)

The draft NodeFrame took 13 props including 4 conditional flags (withLateralHandles, extraClass, drift, diffBadge) plus an extraBadges ReactNode slot, just to accommodate the three call sites. Each future divergence would add another flag that two callers pass as undefined — classic fake-DRY god-component.

resolveDriftBorder(isDrift, styles) is a one-liner (isDrift ? 'border-dashed' : styles.borderStyle). Extracting it adds an import and hides trivial logic.

Actual shared code is ~10 LOC of className strings + handle boilerplate per file, not 30. Not worth the abstraction.

If the className string ever genuinely drifts across the three files, file a surgical bead for a NODE_FRAME_CLASS constant only.
close_reason: Attempted refactor revealed surface duplication is shallow while semantic divergences (drift vs phantom, lateral edges in resource/hierarchy only, bold hierarchy, job nav in resource only) are real. Unified NodeFrame ended up as a 13-prop variant switcher with 4+ conditional flags — fake DRY. Leaving the three files as-is.

title: CLI warnings for dangerous plan actions
description:
Emit warnings for plan actions that have destructive real-world consequences users might not expect.

Priority case: schema recreate. A 'recreate' action on a Unity Catalog schema drops all tables in that schema — this is catastrophic and not obvious from the plan output alone. dagshund should surface a loud warning when it sees this.

Warning categories (start small, expand later):
- Schema recreate → warns about table loss
- Mass deletes (>N resources with action=delete) → warns about blast radius
- Any 'recreate' action → warns that resource will be destroyed and re-created

Output:
- Warnings print above the resource summary in text mode
- Distinct from the diff output — visually separated, maybe with a ⚠ prefix or similar
- Should work with --detailed-exitcode (warnings don't change exit code — or maybe they should? design decision)
- Could later integrate into browser mode as a warnings panel

Start with schema recreate detection. That's the one that bites people.

title: structural-diff: identity-matched array elements skip value comparison
description:
In diffArrays() (structural-diff.ts line 132-139), when array elements are matched by identity key, they are unconditionally marked 'unchanged' without comparing actual values via deepEqual. If two elements share an identity key but have different field values, the diff incorrectly reports no change.

Latent bug — not yet triggered by real plan data because change entries are field-level paths, not whole-array comparisons. But will bite if computeStructuralDiff is ever called with arrays whose identity-matched elements differ.

Fix: call deepEqual(oldItem, item) after identity match. If different, mark as 'modified'. Requires adding 'modified' to ArrayElementStatus and an 'old' field to ArrayElement.

title: docs-only MR short-circuit: skip golden + dependency-scan on .md-only changes
description:
On the three-lane CI model (feat/zfl8), every MR runs the full suite including `golden` (fixture diff) and `dependency-scan` (OSV). README-only or docs/*.md-only MRs pay full freight.

## Proposal

Add a `changes:` filter to `golden` and `dependency-scan` so they skip when the MR touches only Markdown / doc sources that can't affect either signal:

- golden: skip when only `**/*.md`, `.gitignore`, `.editorconfig`, LICENSE change
- dependency-scan: skip when neither `uv.lock` nor `js/bun.lock` changes

Keep `quality` always-on (cheap + broad coverage, sanity-checks docstrings via type hints).

## Out of scope

- `docs/pages/**` is deployed via the main-push `pages` job, so it still needs validation — do NOT lump it in with docs-only.
- The filter must not apply to tag pipelines; tag is defense-in-depth by design.

## Discovered from dagshund-zfl8 review
Senior DevOps pass called this out as a minute-saving opportunity for a personal project on free-tier.

title: for_each_task items show as unchanged despite being changed at resource level
description:
In the browser UI, for_each_task items show as unchanged in the detail panel even though the task change summary badges at the top of the node show them as changed.

Confirmed from fixture data: the for_each_task tasks have library (whl) changes in the changes record (action=update, different old/new values). The task change summary correctly picks these up as modified. But the structural diff in the detail panel compares new_state vs remote_state, and the library paths differ between them — so the structural diff SHOULD show them as different.

This is likely caused by dagshund-1mk4: the libraries array inside for_each_task.task contains objects with a 'whl' key. diffArrays() would try identity-matching these objects, and if it finds a matching key it marks them unchanged without value comparison.

Location: the structural diff view for task details, driven by js/src/utils/structural-diff.ts.

title: Structured search query DSL
description:
Add a lightweight query DSL for combining search filters. Currently search supports three modes (fuzzy, "exact", type:badge) but they're mutually exclusive — you can't combine them.

Potential syntax:
- type:pipeline name:ingest — AND combination of badge + name match
- type:volume status:added — badge + diff state
- name:"exact match" type:job — exact name + badge

Design questions:
- How far to take this? Full boolean (&&, ||, NOT) or just implicit AND of field:value pairs?
- Should status/diff filters (added/modified/removed) be queryable this way too, merging the toolbar filters into the DSL?
- Parser complexity vs. value — the current three-mode dispatch in computeSearchMatchedIds is simple. A DSL parser is more code to maintain.
- Discoverability — how does the user learn the syntax? Placeholder text, tooltip, help popover?

Probably P4 until the simple search feels limiting in practice.

title: Forbid dict[str, Any] outside the parser once typed model lands

Depends on dagshund-161c. Do NOT file or start until 161c lands.

description:

1. use-node-dimming.ts: buildGlowStyle (pure fn at module scope) + the dimming priority cascade (5 booleans -> opacity). Extract to utils/node-dimming.ts.

title: CLI --changes-only flag to suppress unchanged resources
description:
Add diff state filter flags that mirror the browser UI's Added/Modified/Removed toggle buttons.

Flags:
- -a / --added — show only created resources
- -m / --modified — show only updated/recreated/resized/update_id resources
- -r / --removed — show only deleted resources
- -c / --changes-only — shorthand for -a -m -r (all changes, no unchanged)

Flags compose with each other: -a -m shows added + modified.
When --filter DSL ships (dagshund-thdy), these compose as an additional layer.

Behavior:
- No flags = current behavior (show everything)
- With flags: hide resources whose diff state is not in the visible set
- Hide entire type groups where no resources pass the filter
- Group headers show (changed/total) when filtering reduces the count
- Summary line always counts ALL resources (unchanged count is not lost)
- No effect on browser mode (-o) or --detailed-exitcode logic

Implementation:
- Model as a set of visible diff states passed to render_text
- _ActionConfig.changed maps to diff states: create→added, delete→removed, update/recreate/resize/update_id→modified, skip/empty→unchanged
- _print_resource_groups filters entries against the visible set
- CLI parses flags into the set; empty set means show all

title: buildJobIdMap does not index string-typed numeric job IDs
description:
build-plan-graph.ts:209-246 — buildJobIdMap indexes by numeric job_id only. The Zod schema for run_job_task accepts z.union([z.string(), z.number()]) for job_id, so a string numeric ID is theoretically valid.

Investigation (2026-03-14): Live plan output from Databricks CLI v0.288.0 confirms job_id is always int in remote_state (e.g. 949076684616381). The string branch in the union exists for bundle interpolation strings like ${resources.jobs.data_quality_pipeline.id} in new_state, which are handled separately by the typeof === 'string' check in buildRunJobEdges. A string-typed numeric ID is not produced by the API. Closing as unreachable.

title: Clarify Python plan normalization ownership
description:
Context
The Python architecture review found implicit processing-stage contracts. cli.py normalizes resources for detailed exit codes, while terminal.py and markdown.py normalize independently for output. The renderers replace Plan.resources with normalized resources while Plan.raw remains the original redacted input. The same Plan type can therefore carry parsed or normalized resources without making that distinction explicit.

Objective
Establish a clear normalization owner and explicit contracts for parsed plans, normalized resources, and the original redacted payload. Avoid repeated normalization within one CLI invocation without losing the raw payload needed for HTML export.

Scope
- src/dagshund/cli.py, model.py, merge.py, terminal.py, and markdown.py.
- browser.py and provenance.py only as necessary to preserve their input contracts; no browser UI changes.
- Relevant Python orchestration and behavioral tests.

Acceptance criteria
- Resource normalization has a clear orchestration owner, and each relevant function states whether it consumes parsed or normalized resources.
- A CLI invocation that renders stdout and computes detailed exit codes reuses the same normalized resources rather than independently interpreting the plan twice.
- Avoid replacing Plan.resources solely to pass normalized data alongside unrelated envelope metadata. Select the smallest explicit contract that resolves the ambiguity; another dataclass is optional, not a requirement.
- Preserve standalone renderer usability under the chosen explicit contract, updating internal callers and tests consistently rather than keeping an ambiguous mixture of raw and normalized inputs.
- Keep Plan.raw as the original parsed, redacted payload for HTML embedding. Do not serialize normalized resource dataclasses in its place or accidentally discard original entries needed by the HTML consumer.
- Preserve provenance: source digest still reflects the exact input bytes, not the redacted or normalized serialization.
- Preserve lazy optional-feature imports, empty-plan handling, filtering-independent exit codes, subresource merging, effect folding, and terminal/Markdown output.
- Existing golden outputs remain unchanged relative to the baseline after approved semantic corrections. Tests cover stdout-only, quiet detailed-exitcode, stdout plus detailed-exitcode, and combined HTML/stdout paths.
- Follow repository workflow, including just check and just build in the Nix shell for implementation verification.

Constraints and exclusions
No debug tracing changes, parser/schema validation policy changes, new dependencies, generic pipeline framework, broad state-access unification, frontend changes, or forced proliferation of stage types. Coordinate interfaces with the semantics and shared-reporting beads; these are related parts of a bounded improvement, not a mandate for a rewrite.
close_reason: Implemented CLI-owned normalization shared by stdout and detailed exit codes, explicit normalized renderer contracts, and preserved original redacted HTML payload and exact-byte provenance. Quality gates, build, golden outputs, browser verification, and three-pass review completed; approved template-independent regression test fix verified.

title: ci: semgrep parses stale Python/TS grammars — silent coverage gap
description:
GitLab's semgrep SAST analyzer (currently v6.18.0, from registry.gitlab.com/security-products/semgrep:6) ships a semgrep binary whose parsers are behind modern Python and TypeScript grammars. Files that fail to parse are silently skipped — the scan reports "completed successfully" but those files get zero rule coverage.

## Observed on MR 28 (2026-04-17)

semgrep-sast job log, parse warnings:

Python (PEP 634 match/case + PEP 695 `type` statements):
- src/dagshund/types.py:3      — `type ResourceKey = str`
- src/dagshund/filter.py:47    — `type _SearchToken = ...`
- src/dagshund/cli.py:219      — `match args.format:`
- src/dagshund/format.py:95    — `match value:`
- fixtures/tooling/sanitize.py:21 — `type EmailMapping = dict[str, str]`

TypeScript:
- js/src/html-assembler.ts:22  — regex `/<!--/g` confuses the parser; everything after line 22 is dropped (~80 lines of HTML-assembly code, including the DOMPurify-adjacent escape helpers — meaningful from a SAST perspective).

Scan summary in the same log: "Ran 177 rules on 147 files: 0 findings. Parsed lines: ~99.9%." The 0.1% gap = us.

## Version baseline (2026-04-17, via registry probe)

- Tag `:6` = `:6.18` = `:6.18.0` = digest `sha256:d3aecff03d2a7a37f9ebfa396cf25499491e27c31d2ca75030f00b11337de5fe`
- Built 2026-04-09
- semgrep 1.145.0 (`pip install semgrep==$SCANNER_VERSION`, SCANNER_VERSION=1.145.0)
- python 3.12.13 (alpine)
- `:6.17.0` is a distinct older digest; the `:6` floating tag has already rolled forward
- No newer `:6.x` tag exists upstream as of this probe

## What's under our control (done in MR pinning this bead)

1. Digest-pin the analyzer image via `SEMGREP_IMAGE` variable + `image:` override on `semgrep-sast`, matching UV_IMAGE / OSV_SCANNER_IMAGE / ALPINE_IMAGE pattern. Supply-chain hygiene win independent of the parse gap.

## What's not under our control

- semgrep parser support (upstream)
- GitLab's analyzer rebuild cadence (pip install semgrep==SCANNER_VERSION at image build)

## Watch trigger

Re-probe the analyzer digest + semgrep version when any of:
- GitLab bumps the SAST template default analyzer version
- GitLab publishes analyzer v7
- semgrep 1.x releases notes indicate PEP 695 parse support

If the new semgrep version parses all 6 files clean, bump the `SEMGREP_IMAGE` digest pin and close this bead.

title: detail panel: add 'Removed on apply' section symmetric to 'Re-added on apply'; frame both as drift
description:
## Observed (post dagshund-1naj)

In the detail panel, clicking the `publish` task of the manual-drift fixture shows two semantically parallel drift events rendered with very different UI weight:

    Re-added on apply
    Present in your bundle but missing from the remote — will be recreated on apply.
    + depends_on[task_key='transform']
    +   task_key: transform

    Removed
    depends_on[task_key='ingest']  [drift][delete]
    (drift)
    - task_key: ingest

- **Re-added on apply** has its own section, explanatory prose, and an `+` item. It's the existing topology-drift renderer with a dedicated story.
- **Removed** is the generic delete bucket. The reclassified-as-drift delete (from dagshund-1naj) gets a drift pill and `(drift)` tag, but no section-level framing of what apply will do.

Both events have the same semantic: a manual edit the bundle will overwrite. The UI renders them asymmetrically.

## Proposal

### 1. Add a dedicated "Removed on apply" section

Parallel structure to "Re-added on apply": its own section, own prose, groups reclassified-drift deletes.

    Removed on apply (drift)
    Present on the remote but missing from your bundle — will be removed on apply.
    If this was unintentional, add it back to your bundle.
    - depends_on[task_key='ingest']
    -   task_key: ingest

Qualifying entries: changes where `extractListElementSemantic` returned `"delete"` AND `resourceHasShapeDrift` is true (the same gate that already tags them drift in `computeStructuralDiff`).

Non-drift deletes (e.g. plain `has_old`, no_new, no_remote shape in create/delete-family resources) stay in the generic "Removed" section.

### 2. Frame both sections as drift explicitly

Make the drift framing explicit in the section labels and prose, not just via the drift pill on individual entries.

Current prose on "Re-added on apply":
> Present in your bundle but missing from the remote — will be recreated on apply.

Proposed:
> **Re-added on apply (drift)**
> Present in your bundle but missing from the remote — someone removed it manually, apply will re-add it.

Proposed for new section:
> **Removed on apply (drift)**
> Present on the remote but missing from your bundle — someone added it manually, apply will remove it.

The explicit "someone … manually" framing tells the user WHY this will happen, not just what.

## Why now

dagshund-1naj surfaced a new class of drift events (reclassified list-element deletes) that land in the generic Removed bucket. This asymmetry was less visible before because:
- Pre-1naj, these entries were misclassified as `(remote)` and hidden in the Modified section — no user could see them at all.
- The "Re-added on apply" renderer pre-dates 1naj and has always had its own section.

Now that 1naj exposes both directions, the imbalance is visible.

## Relationship to dagshund-qby2

dagshund-qby2 proposes unifying the per-entry tag vocabulary (`(drift)` / `(re-added)` → verb-explicit like `(will re-add)` / `(will remove)`). This bead operates one level up: section structure and prose. They're complementary:

- **qby2** fixes inconsistent per-entry tags.
- **3hdx (this bead)** fixes inconsistent section-level structure.

Ideally land together. If staged: qby2 first (tag vocab stable) → 3hdx (section restructure using the stabilized vocab).

Alternative to consider: collapse both into a single unified "Drift" section with re-add and remove sub-groups. Lower total UI surface, single place for the drift prose. Trade-off: larger departure from current structure; users who know "Re-added on apply" will need to re-learn. Recommend sticking with Option A (parallel sections) for continuity.

## Scope

- `js/src/components/detail-panel/` — locate the topology-drift "Re-added on apply" renderer (likely `drift-body.tsx` or inside a parent body component). Add a parallel "Removed on apply" renderer.
- `modified-body.tsx` — stop routing reclassified-drift deletes to "Removed"; route them to the new section instead. Gate: `derived action === "delete"` AND `ctx.resourceHasShapeDrift === true`.
- Update prose on both sections per proposal #2.
- Tests: `modified-body.test.tsx` — add cases asserting routing + new section appearance.

## Out of scope

- Python terminal/markdown — flat output, no sections.
- The generic "Removed" section stays for non-drift deletes (standard delete-action shape in a resource being deleted entirely).

## Devil's advocate

*Does every reclassified drift delete deserve a section?* If there's only one, a full section + prose is overkill. Counter: same concern applies to "Re-added on apply" today (a single re-add also gets the full treatment). Consistency wins.

*Will users find "Removed on apply (drift)" confusing when there's also a plain "Removed" section?* Maybe. The two sections answer different questions: "bundle is deleting this" vs "apply is undoing someone's manual addition." The distinction is real and worth naming. The `(drift)` suffix on the section label is the disambiguator.

*Is this a UX call that should wait for a design pass across the whole panel?* Possibly. But the current state is actively worse (asymmetric, harder for a user to form a mental model). Shipping either A or B improves on "do nothing."

## Related

- dagshund-1naj — bug fix that surfaced this asymmetry
- dagshund-qby2 — vocabulary unification (per-entry tags)
- dagshund-93lv — topology-drift duplication in Unchanged section

title: CI hygiene: just recipe drift, stale workflow comment, weekly security scan
description:
Three CI maintenance items bundled. Do in any order; each stands alone.

## 1. Fix stale workflow comment (trivial)

`.gitlab-ci.yml:21-26` describes the three-lane model but claims tag pushes only run `release (version-check, build, smoke-wheel, publish)`. In reality `secret_detection` (`.gitlab-ci.yml:46-54`) and `dependency-scan` (`.gitlab-ci.yml:59-73`) both re-run on tags for defense in depth. Update the comment so it matches the job rules.

## 2. `just` recipe drift between dev and CI

CI `build` job manually replicates `just build` (bun build:template, cp SKILL.md, uv build). The UV_IMAGE doesn't ship `just`, so we can't simply call `just build`. As the build recipe grows (Tailwind bumps, asset hashing, new assets), drift between justfile and CI becomes a maintenance tax.

### Options

- **A. Extract `scripts/build-wheel.sh`.** Both `just build` and CI call the same script. No `just` needed in CI, zero new binaries. Likely the right answer.
- **B. Cache the `just` binary in CI.** Download + SHA256-verify `casey/just` releases, cache keyed on JUST_VERSION (mirrors the existing Bun pattern). Pro: CI runs the literal `just build` command. Con: another pinned version to bump, another cache key.
- **C. Status quo + drift-detection grep.** Ugly, not recommended.

Pick A or B based on whether \"CI runs the same command devs run\" is worth the bun-style caching ceremony. If the build recipe stays small, A wins. If it grows to include dev-only bells (watchers, formatters, test-triggers), B keeps the CI surface stable.

Related: dagshund-2omy (tooling bumps) — doing this first means `just` becomes one more pinned version to track under item 3.

## 3. Weekly scheduled pipeline: dep scan + tooling-update check

Add a scheduled pipeline (cron: Sunday UTC) that:

- Re-runs `dependency-scan` (OSV-Scanner against uv.lock + js/bun.lock) to catch CVE disclosures landing against unchanged lockfiles between releases.
- Reports tooling versions that have newer releases available — analogous to Dependabot/Renovate but kept lightweight. Options:
  - **Simple:** one job runs `uv pip list --outdated` + `bun outdated` and fails (or opens an issue via glab) if anything is behind.
  - **Renovate Bot:** GitLab-friendly, full MR automation. Heavier setup, more noise, but handles the full loop including the MR open.
  - **Custom:** small script comparing pinned versions (UV_IMAGE, BUN_VERSION, JUST_VERSION if B is chosen) against upstream release feeds, piped into a scheduled GitLab issue.

### Wiring

Top-level `workflow:` rules need a new case: `$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == \"schedule\"`. Schedule itself configured in GitLab UI (Settings → CI/CD → Schedules) with a Sunday cron. Jobs that should run under schedule get a matching rule.

Start with the simple version (outdated-report job) — can always upgrade to Renovate later if the manual triage becomes annoying.

title: Make project guidance agent-neutral
description:
## Problem

Durable project workflow and engineering guidance lives under .claude/, especially .claude/CLAUDE.md and .claude/WORKFLOW.md. Claude reads that context, but other agents do not reliably discover it. This caused real friction: a non-Claude agent missed the Beads workflow and inspected .beads/issues.jsonl directly instead of using br.

The repo should expose its project rules through an agent-neutral entry point while keeping tool-specific files as thin compatibility shims.

## Proposed direction

- Add a root-level AGENTS.md as the canonical guidance file for AI coding agents.
- Move or copy durable, agent-agnostic rules there: br workflow, session start expectations, just command usage, git/MR rules, quality gates, project philosophy, and pointers to language-specific guidance.
- Keep .claude/CLAUDE.md as a Claude-specific shim that references AGENTS.md and any Claude-only mechanics.
- Decide whether .claude/WORKFLOW.md remains canonical, becomes included from AGENTS.md, or is reduced to a Claude-specific adapter.
- Consider adding short notes for other agents/tools if needed, but avoid duplicating long guidance in multiple places.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fresh non-Claude agent can discover the workflow from the repository root without knowing to inspect .claude/.
- The Beads rule is prominent: use br for issues, do not manually edit .beads/issues.jsonl, mark work in progress, and close beads only after the work is actually complete.
- Developer commands remain centralized around just, with the no-direct-pytest/ruff/biome/tsc convention preserved.
- Claude still has a valid CLAUDE.md entry point, but it delegates shared rules to the agent-neutral source.
- Duplication is minimized enough that workflow changes do not need to be patched in three places.
- No behavior/code changes; docs and agent-guidance structure only.
notes: Implemented in MR !49: AGENTS.md root guide, docs/guidelines move, docs/workflows neutral runbooks, Claude command shims under .claude/commands, and repo-local Codex skill shims under .codex/skills. User-level ~/.codex/skills symlinks were removed; project-local .codex/skills is the tracked source.

title: Add real Lakebase and enterprise-resource golden fixtures
description:
Databricks Free Edition now has Lakebase available, and dagshund still needs genuine golden fixture coverage for resource types currently represented only by synthetic or enterprise-only plans. Merge of dagshund-3l7p and dagshund-ry3b.

## Scope

Add one or more real golden fixtures covering Lakebase and enterprise-tier resource types from actual Databricks bundle plan output instead of relying only on hand-authored synthetic coverage.

Resource families to cover where workspace tier and Databricks availability allow:
- Lakebase/database resources available in Free Edition
- catalogs
- database_catalogs
- database_instances
- postgres_projects
- postgres_branches
- postgres_endpoints
- synced_database_tables
- external_locations

## Deliverables

- before/after bundle configs for regenerable fixtures where possible
- regenerated plan.json from real DAB output
- expected text, markdown, exit-code, and graph outputs
- fixture docs updated with any new workspace prerequisites or tier requirements
- clear split between Free Edition-regenerable coverage and enterprise-only coverage if both cannot live in one fixture

## Context

Free Edition Lakebase availability was discovered during Databricks CLI 0.299.2 fixture regeneration. The older enterprise fixture bead noted that all-hierarchies covers enterprise-only resource types but is hand-authored and cannot be regenerated via just regen without a real enterprise workspace.

## Acceptance criteria

- just gen-expected <fixture> and just test-golden work for any committed regenerable fixture.
- Any non-regenerable or enterprise-only fixture limitations are documented explicitly.
- Synthetic-only coverage for these resource families is reduced or clearly justified.
- Close dagshund-ry3b as merged into this bead.

extractResourceName returns last segment instead of full dotted name
description:
resource-key.ts:2-5 returns segments[segments.length - 1], so resources.jobs.data.pipeline → 'pipeline'. Python's parse_resource_key correctly joins remaining segments: 'data.pipeline'. This affects node labels in the resource graph and causes a search DSL parity gap.

Investigation (2026-03-14): Dotted YAML resource keys (e.g. etl_pipeline.hey.hot.pop) pass databricks bundle validate but crash the CLI with a nil pointer dereference in ResourceJob.PrepareState (job.go:51) on both plan and deploy. The CLI never produces plan JSON with dotted keys — dagshund would never see them. Additionally, UC object names cannot contain dots per Unity Catalog naming rules. Closing as unreachable.

Reference: Databricks CLI v0.288.0 panic in dresources.(*ResourceJob).PrepareState — could be filed as a bug at https://github.com/databricks/cli but is unlikely to be 'fixed' by allowing dots.

title: policy: drop Python 3.12 floor, pin requires-python >=3.13?
description:
Policy decision, not a tooling bump. Decide whether to raise the Python floor.

## Current state
- pyproject.toml: requires-python = ">=3.12"
- classifiers list 3.12, 3.13, 3.14
- CI pytest logs show 3.14 is the runtime

## Question
Drop 3.12 and pin to >=3.13? Or >=3.14 to match CI?

## Tradeoffs
- Narrower floor = fewer environments to support, can use newer stdlib features
- Wider floor = more users can install via uvx dagshund (PyPI distribution matters here)
- We have zero runtime Python deps, so the floor is purely about stdlib/syntax availability
- End-of-life timeline: 3.12 EOL 2028-10, 3.13 EOL 2029-10, 3.14 EOL 2030-10

## Steps
1. Search src/dagshund for any 3.13+ syntax we're already using
2. Decide
3. Update requires-python + classifiers if raising

title: audit codebase for old-style depends_on[N] handling
description:
Databricks CLI 0.298.0 (PR https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/4990, a bug we reported that got fixed) changed how `depends_on` is represented in `plan.json` diff entries.

**Old format (index-based):**
  "key": "tasks[task_key='publish'].depends_on[0].task_key", "action": "update"

**New format (key-based):**
  "key": "tasks[task_key='publish'].depends_on[task_key='ingest']", "action": "update"

The fix surfaced while regenerating golden fixtures for 0.298.0 (see dagshund-1b66). Dagshund's rendered output now describes depends_on changes more accurately — unchanged deps stay as "(remote)", re-added deps show as "(re-added)" — instead of presenting them as a scalar swap like `depends_on[0].task_key: \"ingest\" -> \"transform\"`.

## What to check

1. Any remaining parsing/rendering code that assumes `depends_on[\d+]` index-style keys — grep for `depends_on\[` patterns in src/dagshund (Python) and js/src (TS).
2. Test fixtures or unit tests that hardcode the old index shape (e.g. in JS change-diff tests, Python summary tests).
3. Whether the output improvement is worth surfacing in the CHANGELOG for the next release.
4. If old plan.json files in the wild (from users on CLI <= 0.297.x) still render correctly — both shapes may need to be supported for a transition period, or we document that dagshund targets CLI >= 0.298.0.

## Why

This is a semantically meaningful upstream fix that dagshund is passively surfacing. Worth a pass to confirm nothing downstream made assumptions about the old shape, and to decide whether to flag it in release notes.
close_reason: Audit complete. Found one actionable issue (detail-panel grouping) — filed as dagshund-1naj with full repro, root cause, and fix direction. No code changes needed for depends_on parsing/rendering outside of that bug: the generic change-path parser legitimately handles both [0] and [task_key='...'] shapes; the graph builder already diffs from remote_state sets directly; Python terminal/markdown renderers are flat (no grouping bug); all goldens already use the new key-based shape. CHANGELOG note for CLI >= 0.298.0 recommendation deferred to next release.

comments.author: 6337146-chinchy@users.noreply.gitlab.com
comments.text:
## UI observation: detail panel renders the `publish` task's depends_on drift as

**Re-added on apply** (Present in your bundle but missing from the remote — will be recreated on apply.)

    + depends_on[task_key='transform']
    +   task_key: transform

**Modified**

    depends_on[task_key='ingest']  remote
    =  task_key: ingest

## The awkwardness

The "Modified" section lists `depends_on[task_key='ingest']` with a single `=` row meaning "matches remote". That's a no-op inside a section titled "Modified". Worth checking whether the detail panel should:

1. Drop equality-only entries from "Modified" entirely (they're just context, not actual edits).
2. Or keep them but rename the section / visually de-emphasize so "Modified" doesn't falsely imply a change.

The audit in this bead should include the detail-panel grouping logic, not just the parsing/rendering pass.

comments.author: 6337146-chinchy@users.noreply.gitlab.com
comments.text:
## Additional UI observation: mixed-changes renders a fresh depends_on add as

**Modified**

    depends_on[task_key='anomaly_detection']  create
    +  task_key: anomaly_detection

Under the "Modified" section, but the row is a pure create (`+`) with a `create` badge. Same grouping issue as the manual-drift `ingest` row — "Modified" is being used as a catch-all bucket for any entry whose sub-rows aren't all equality. A brand-new dep showing up under "Modified" reads wrong; it should be in an "Added" (or "Created") group so the section title matches the content.

Worth treating this and the manual-drift observation as the same underlying issue in the audit: the detail-panel grouping is too coarse post-fix. The old CLI collapsed these into scalar swaps ("Modified" was accurate then); the new CLI gives us per-dep create/remove/equal, so the panel should group accordingly.

comments.author: 6337146-chinchy@users.noreply.gitlab.com
comments.text:
## task-dag-rewiring: the clearest case that dagshund was passively propagating CLI bugs

Under old CLI output, dagshund was rendering three classes of wrong-ish content that have cleaned up under 0.298.0:

1. **Fake changes on reorders.**
   Old: `combine.depends_on[0].task_key: "process_a" -> "process_b"` + `[1].task_key: "process_b" -> "process_a"` flagged as two edits. But deps are a set, so swapping positions is a no-op.
   New: combine's depends_on entries disappear entirely. Correct.

2. **Lossy array summaries.**
   Old: `publish.depends_on: [2 items] -> [{task_key: "full_validation"}]` — couldn't see which of the 2 items was removed without drilling in.
   New: `- publish.depends_on[task_key='skip_validation']` — explicit.

3. **Misleading scalar framing for set diffs.**
   Old: `process_b.depends_on[0].task_key: "clean" -> "ingest"` + `[1].task_key: "filter" -> "validate"` read like 2 scalar edits. Actual semantics: remove {clean, filter}, add {ingest, validate}.
   New: 4 explicit entries for remove clean/filter + add ingest/validate.

## Audit implication

The audit should frame dagshund's role here as a passive renderer: we pass through whatever the CLI emits. When the CLI had bugs, we inherited them. The fix is upstream, but the audit should still:

- Check if any dagshund logic special-cased the old lossy/scalar shapes (e.g. heuristics for "is this a reorder vs a real change") — those can now be deleted as the CLI handles it correctly.
- Confirm the graph-builder's dedup / merge logic still behaves correctly now that `depends_on` is emitted as per-key entries instead of sometimes scalar, sometimes array.
- Treat the detail-panel grouping fix (earlier comments) as higher priority than it looks: the new shape makes the old "Modified" bucket obviously wrong.

title: Fix action:null inconsistency across three functions
description:
## Problem

Three functions in `src/dagshund/text.py` disagree on how to interpret `"action": null` (JSON null / Python None) in a resource entry, producing inconsistent output.

## The Three Functions and Their Behavior

### 1. `_render_resource` (around line 101)
- Uses `entry.get("action", "")` → returns `None` (not the default, because key exists with value None)
- `_display_action(None)` → returns `None` unchanged (not in `_DISPLAY_ACTIONS`, falls through)
- Resource displayed as `? jobs/test  (None)` with unknown-action style

### 2. `_count_by_action` (around line 138)
- Uses `entry.get("action") or "unchanged"` → `None or "unchanged"` → `"unchanged"`
- Summary counts it as "unchanged"

### 3. `_all_unchanged` (around line 194)
- Uses `entry.get("action", "")` → returns `None`
- Checks `None in ("skip", "")` → `False`
- So it does NOT consider the resource unchanged, meaning the full resource listing is shown

## Result
- Summary line says "unchanged"
- Resource listing shows "?/None" with unknown-action styling
- `_all_unchanged` says "not all unchanged" so the listing IS shown (contradicting the summary)

## Reproduction
```python
from dagshund.text import render_text
import json
render_text(json.dumps({"plan": {"resources.jobs.test": {"action": None}}}))
```

## Design Decision Needed
What should `action: null` mean? Options:
1. Treat it the same as `action: ""` and `action: "skip"` → "unchanged"
2. Treat it as an unknown/error action

Either way, all three functions must agree. Recommendation: treat null the same as missing/empty → "unchanged", since Databricks CLI may omit the field or set it to null for no-op resources.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All three functions (`_render_resource`, `_count_by_action`, `_all_unchanged`) handle `action: null` consistently
- The chosen behavior is explicit, not accidental (e.g., normalize early rather than relying on falsy checks)
- `just check` passes
close_reason: Aligned _count_by_action to use same extraction pattern as _render_resource and _all_unchanged — null actions now consistently treated as unknown

title: Add missing task type badges: clean_rooms_notebook, dashboard, power_bi

title: Add unit tests for 3 untested pure functions
description:
Three pure exported functions lack isolated unit tests. All are indirectly exercised through integration tests but have no direct proof of correctness.

## Functions

1. **resolveLateralContext** — `js/src/utils/connected-nodes.ts:64` (31 lines)
   - Builds lateral dependency context from edges for the detail panel
   - Its siblings (buildConnectedNodeIds, resolvePhantomContext) are tested in the same file
   - Test cases: empty edges, depends-on only, depended-on-by only, both directions, non-lateral edge filtering, missing node references

2. **toEdgeDiffState** — `js/src/types/graph-types.ts:57` (2 lines)
   - Maps DiffState to EdgeDiffState (drops 'modified' → 'unchanged')

title: chore: clean dist/ before build
description: dist/ accumulates stale build artifacts (80+ files observed). Source maps could expose source code if dist/ were accidentally shared. Fix: add 'rm -rf dist &&' to the build script in package.json.

title: Define scope and priorities for next features
description: Discussion task: define what the user wants in the visualizer before building more. Topics may include graph layout, React Flow rendering, UI/UX, interaction model, file upload vs stdin, etc.
close_reason: Scope defined: graph model (dagshund-ebk) → rendering (dagshund-qu9) + stdin (dagshund-1z4) in parallel. PyDABS testing tracked as dagshund-5f6 backlog.

title: fix: clean up modified task detail panel — remove redundant diff state display
description:
The detail panel for modified tasks is visually noisy with redundant information:

## Current behavior
- Top bar shows task name + "modified" action badge
- Below that, a "Modified" text banner repeats the same info
- Then the actual changed fields
- Then an "Unchanged" separator at the bottom

## Desired behavior
- Top bar: task name + "modified" action badge (keep as-is)
- Body: "Modified" and "Unchanged" section dividers organizing the fields
- No extra banner/block that redundantly restates the diff state

Added and removed nodes are clean — single wrapped block with a tag. Modified tasks should follow the same clean pattern but with section dividers to separate changed vs unchanged fields.

title: Smarter diff display for modified resources in detail panel
description:
When clicking a modified node, the detail panel currently shows full before/after arrays for fields like depends_on. For example:

- [{ task_key: check_nulls }]
+ [{ task_key: check_nulls }, { task_key: check_duplicates }]

This should be reduced to just showing the meaningful delta:
+ check_duplicates

However, this is not always straightforward — need to think about validity/edge cases:
- What if items were reordered but not added/removed?
- What if items were both added AND removed in the same array?
- What about arrays of primitives vs arrays of objects?
- How do we match identity across old/new arrays (by which key)?
- Nested object diffs within array items

Needs a design pass before implementation to handle these cases correctly.

title: epic: UI overhaul — Databricks-inspired design with dark/light mode
description:
Graphical overhaul of the entire application to bring a cohesive, polished visual style inspired by the Databricks UI aesthetic.

## Goals
- Adopt a Databricks-inspired design language (clean lines, subtle shadows, professional color palette)
- Implement both dark mode and light mode with a user toggle
- Consistent styling across all views (DAG, resources, detail panel, upload screen)

## Scope
- Theming infrastructure (CSS variables or Tailwind theme, mode toggle, persistence)
- Restyle all components: nodes, edges, panels, buttons, inputs, headers
- Diff state colors adapted for both modes (green/red/amber must be readable in both)
- React Flow canvas styling (background, controls, minimap)
- Typography, spacing, and layout polish

title: Add YAML/JSON toggle button in detail panel
description: Add a toggle button in the detail panel to switch between YAML-formatted and raw JSON display for resource state and diff values. Currently shows JSON via formatValue().

title: render Postgres role and database lateral edges
description: In the reported Databricks CLI 1.8.0 plan, postgres_roles.consumer_engineers and postgres_roles.elevated_engineers do not render lateral edges to postgres_databases.shared_database, while postgres_roles.dsh_owner does. The current graph derives only the explicit database.role reference, which points to dsh_owner; the other roles share resources.postgres_branches.production but have no direct database field. Investigate the intended Lakebase semantics before implementing. Determine whether every role and database on the same branch should be connected, including behavior when a branch has multiple databases, or whether another plan field should drive the relationship. Add a regression case based on the supplied plan once the rule is confirmed.
close_reason: Not a bug: all Postgres roles are branch children, while only the required database owner role has the additional explicit database.role lateral relationship.

title: Add pipeline/job write-target highlighting as toggle feature
description: Pipelines and jobs write to UC locations (catalog/schema/target fields) but these aren't hierarchy relationships. Could be a toggle feature where selecting a pipeline or job highlights both the resource and where it writes to. Pipeline fields: catalog, schema, target, event_log.catalog, event_log.schema, ingestion_definition.objects[].destination_catalog/schema.
close_reason: Consolidated into dagshund-czfs (toggle for non-hierarchy relationships)

title: chore: add missing barrel exports to types/index.ts
description: R3-LOW-29. Several exported types are missing from the types/index.ts barrel: TaskChangeSummaryEntry (from graph-types.ts), BaselineLabel (from structural-diff.ts), ArrayElementStatus (from structural-diff.ts). Consumers must import directly from module files instead of the barrel. Fix: add these to the re-exports in types/index.ts. Flagged by: Code Quality (MEDIUM/LOW).

title: Test dagshund with PyDABS-generated bundle plans
description: Validate that dagshund correctly parses and visualizes plan JSON generated from PyDABS dynamic bundle definitions. PyDABS generates Databricks asset bundle YAML dynamically, which then feeds into databricks bundle plan. Ensure the plan output from these dynamically-generated bundles renders correctly — edge cases may include unusual resource structures or dependency patterns that static YAML wouldn't produce.

title: Use hatchling dynamic versioning instead of dual version
description: Version is hardcoded in both __init__.py and pyproject.toml. Use hatchling's [tool.hatch.version] to read from __init__.py dynamically, eliminating the second source of truth.

title: Show sync relationship context on phantom sync-target nodes in detail panel
description:
Phantom sync-target nodes (e.g. sync-target::dagshund.analytics.customer_360) show an empty or unhelpful detail panel when clicked. These nodes exist because a synced_database_table references them as its UC destination.

The detail panel should show:
- That this is a sync target
- Which synced_database_table(s) sync to it (e.g. 'Sync target of: customer_360')
- The resource type of the source (synced_database_table)

Without this context, clicking a phantom sync-target node gives no indication of what it is or why it exists.

description: cli.ts inlines CSS into <style> tag without escaping </style sequences. If CSS ever contained </style, it would break out. Fix: add .replace(/<\/style/gi, '<\/style') to CSS before inlining, same pattern as the script tag escaping.

title: Type safety: add comments to all as casts, replace any with typed import
description:
Five type safety findings from TS review:

1. **6 uncommented as casts in flow-canvas.tsx** (lines 160, 168, 176, 200, 266, 267): Casts from readonly to mutable for React Flow API compatibility. Add comment explaining why on each.

2. **let mod: any in layout-graph.test.ts** (line 13): Dynamic import workaround uses any, disabling all type checking. Replace with typeof import('...') so test assertions are type-checked.

3. **Uncommented as cast in use-stdin-plan.ts** (line 17): Window augmentation cast needs a comment explaining why.

4. **Un-narrowed union in detail-panel.tsx** (lines 59-61, 107): data.taskChangeSummary accessed after boolean guard that TypeScript can't narrow through. Either inline the check or use a type predicate function so the compiler tracks the narrowing.

5. **Uncommented as casts in test files** (build-resource-graph.test.ts, layout-graph.test.ts): Discriminated union narrowing casts in tests. Add brief comments.

title: Lateral edge for quality_monitor table_name → UC table
description:
Quality monitors have a required table_name field — a three-part UC name (catalog.schema.table) identifying the table being monitored. There is no lateral edge from quality_monitor → UC table.

The lateral-deps fixture has a quality_monitor (table_monitor) with table_name: dagshund.phantom_schema.phantom_table. Note: warehouse_id is in new_state but NOT in remote_state for this resource.

Needs:
- Parse table_name as a three-part UC name
- Resolve against UC chain hierarchy nodes (catalog::, schema::, or source-table::)
- Lateral edge from quality_monitor → resolved UC node(s)
- Phantom nodes via UC chain if targets are absent
- Verify with: just gen-expected lateral-deps && just test-golden

title: fix: simplify job detail panel in resources tab
description: When clicking a job node on the Resources tab, the detail panel is overwhelming. It shows the full Modified section with all task-level changes (depends_on diffs, new tasks, field changes) AND the full Unchanged section with every field (deployment, environments, all tasks with their full config). This is too much for the Resources tab — the Jobs tab already provides the detailed task-level DAG view. The Resources tab should show a condensed summary for jobs: just the top-level resource state (name, format, max_concurrent_runs, etc.) and a high-level change summary (e.g. '3 tasks added, 2 tasks modified') with a link/button to navigate to the Jobs tab for full details.

title: fix: add assertion that __DAGSHUND_PLAN_JSON__ placeholder was actually replaced
description: R3-MED-9. The Python/JS boundary uses a stringly-typed placeholder __DAGSHUND_PLAN_JSON__ in template HTML. Python does .replace() to inject real JSON. If the placeholder string changes in build-template.ts but not in browser.py (or vice versa), the replacement silently fails — the app loads but shows a parse error. Fix: in browser.py _inject_plan, add an assertion that the placeholder is no longer present in the output after replacement. Also consider adding a test that verifies the round-trip works. The placeholder is defined in browser.py:7 and build-template.ts:8. Flagged by: Architect (MEDIUM).

title: refactor: split detail-panel.tsx into directory
description: detail-panel.tsx is 482 lines with 16 co-located components (ActionBadge, DiffStateBadge, ChangeEntry, ResourceStateView, SectionDivider, ObjectStateCard, TaskChangesSummary, etc). CLAUDE.md says each component in its own file. Extract into components/detail-panel/ directory with index.tsx as the main export.

title: fix: make deepEqual key-order-independent in structural-diff
description: structural-diff.ts:12 uses JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b) for deep equality. JSON.stringify is key-order-dependent, so {a:1,b:2} != {b:2,a:1}. This can produce false negatives (phantom diffs) when plan JSON has different key ordering. Also O(n^2) when used in diffArrays findIndex loop. Fix: use a proper key-order-independent deep-equal, and consider building a Map for the fallback matching instead of O(n*m) findIndex.

title: Implement Zod parser + types for plan JSON
Show inference context on phantom nodes in detail panel
description: Phantom/external nodes (dashed border) currently show 'not tracked' with no context. They should surface why they exist — e.g. 'Inferred from resources.volumes.raw_data (schema_name: analytics)' or 'Sync target of resources.synced_database_tables.customer_360'. This helps users understand the graph without needing to know the internal resolution logic. Applies to phantom schemas, phantom branches, phantom catalog groups, phantom instances, and sync-target table nodes.

title: Simplify ResourceChangesByType to compose with ResourceChanges
description: ResourceChangesByType is currently dict[ResourceType, list[tuple[ResourceKey, ResourceChange]]] but could be dict[ResourceType, ResourceChanges] — sub-dicts instead of lists of tuples. The tuple form exists because groupby yields pairs, but building sub-dicts would make the types compose naturally and simplify _print_resource_groups to iterate .items() instead of a tuple list.

title: render generated pipelines for Postgres synced tables
description:
A `postgres_synced_tables` bundle resource creates a managed pipeline in addition to the synced-table resource, but the resource graph does not represent that generated pipeline. The missing output becomes especially visible when a first-deploy job `pipeline_task` references it as `${resources.postgres_synced_tables.<name>.pipeline_id}`: Dagshund treats the symbolic value as an unresolved external pipeline and renders a dashed phantom labelled with the raw interpolation.

The existing first-deploy pipeline resolution only handles `${resources.pipelines.<name>.id}`. Its parser and target resolution do not cover the `pipeline_id` output of `postgres_synced_tables`, and resolving the job edge directly to the owning synced-table node would still hide the real managed pipeline created by the bundle.

Expected behavior:
- Represent the pipeline managed by each `postgres_synced_tables` resource as a derived, non-phantom pipeline node even when no job references it.
- Connect the owning Postgres synced-table resource to its generated pipeline with clear managed-output semantics.
- Resolve valid `${resources.postgres_synced_tables.<name>.pipeline_id}` job task references to that generated pipeline node when the owner exists in the plan.
- Do not create an interpolation-labelled phantom for a resolvable managed pipeline output.
- Preserve ordinary `${resources.pipelines.<name>.id}` resolution, API-ID resolution, and genuine external-pipeline phantoms.
- Define stable identity and labeling for first-deploy plans where the concrete pipeline ID is not available yet, and use concrete new or remote state when available.
- Preserve owner navigation, inherited create/update/delete state, phantom filtering behavior, raw-plan detail semantics, search, and layout conventions used by other managed outputs.
- Cover generated-output extraction, phantom suppression, lateral-edge extraction, resource-graph behavior, first deploy, delete/remote state, missing or malformed IDs, and a representative golden fixture.

Discovered from the Postgres synced-table graph while working on dagshund-hw3o.

title: Conduct full codebase review
description: Comprehensive review of the entire codebase — Python and TypeScript — before setting up CI/CD. Ensures code quality issues are resolved and patterns are consistent before locking them into a pipeline.
close_reason: Replaced with separate Python and TS review beads

title: Add test infrastructure and parser tests
Plan comparison mode (dagshund diff)
description:
Compare two plan JSON files and show what changed between them.

Use case: iterating on bundle config, running plan repeatedly, wanting to see what's different between attempts ('I fixed the config, what changed?').

Needs design decisions before implementation:
- Subcommand (dagshund diff a.json b.json) vs flag (dagshund --diff a.json b.json)
- What 'diff of diffs' means: resource appeared/disappeared, action changed (skip→update), field-level changes shifted
- Text output format for comparison
- Whether browser mode gets a comparison view too
- How to handle plan version/serial mismatches

Park this until --changes-only (dagshund-37yu) ships and we have more real-world usage patterns to inform the design.

title: resolve first-deploy pipeline task references
description:
A job with a pipeline_task targeting a pipeline created in the same bundle is rendered with a phantom pipeline named after the raw interpolation, for example `${resources.pipelines.autocdc_ibmi_mysite_msv542.id}`, instead of resolving to the real pipeline resource.

Observed plan evidence:
- The pipeline resource key is `resources.pipelines.autocdc_ibmi_mysite_msv542`.
- Its create entry exposes the deployed name `autocdc_ibmi_mysite_msv542_nop` in `new_state.value.name`.
- The dependency metadata references the same resource with label `${resources.pipelines.autocdc_ibmi_mysite_msv542.id}`.
- On first deploy, the job task's `pipeline_task.pipeline_id` may carry that symbolic interpolation before an API pipeline ID exists.

Current behavior:
- `extractTaskPipelineId` returns the interpolation as an ordinary string.
- `pipelineIndex` cannot map it because a newly created pipeline has no remote API ID yet.
- Phantom collection then creates `pipeline::${resources.pipelines....id}` and uses the raw interpolation as its display label.
- Lateral edge extraction targets that phantom instead of the real `resources.pipelines.*` node.

Expected behavior:
- Parse a valid `${resources.pipelines.<name>.id}` pipeline task reference and resolve it directly to that real pipeline resource when present.
- Do not materialize an interpolation-labeled phantom for a resolvable bundle reference.
- Preserve existing API-ID resolution and external-pipeline phantom behavior.
- Cover first-deploy symbolic pipeline references in phantom collection, lateral-edge extraction, and resource-graph tests or a representative golden fixture.

Related precedent:
- `resolve-run-job-target.ts` already resolves first-deploy `${resources.jobs.<name>.id}` references for `run_job_task`.
- `extractBundleResourceIdRef` already parses bundle resource interpolations for other resource-reference paths.

title: graph: show Lakebase branch source lineage
description:
Lakebase Postgres branches expose two distinct relationships in plan state. The parent field is hierarchy/containment, e.g. parent: projects/dagshund means the branch belongs under the Lakebase project. A branch created from another branch exposes lineage separately via source_branch, e.g. source_branch: projects/dagshund/branches/prd.

Current resource graph correctly models hierarchy as project -> branches. It did not show source_branch lineage, so a dev branch cloned from prd appeared only as a sibling with no visual relationship to prd.

Implement this as a lateral dependency edge, not a hierarchy edge and not a depends_on edge. The source should be the branch entry that declares source_branch, and the target should be the referenced source branch. This follows existing lateral-edge semantics: the declaring resource points to the resource it semantically depends on.

Expected behavior:
- Preserve project -> branch hierarchy for postgres_branches.parent.
- Parse semantic source_branch paths like projects/<project>/branches/<branch>.
- Resolve source_branch to a real postgres_branches resource node when present in the plan.
- Use phantom branch fallback only if that matches existing lateral-edge conventions and does not clutter the graph; otherwise skip unresolved lineage and document that choice.
- Do not use depends_on to infer lineage.
- Add focused JS tests covering dev -> prd lineage from source_branch while both branches remain siblings under postgres-root/project.

Fixture context: fixtures/golden/lakebase-autoscaling/plan.json has resources.postgres_branches.dev_branch with source_branch: projects/dagshund/branches/prd and parent: projects/dagshund.
close_reason: done: delivered in completed Lakebase fixture and graph work

title: fix: remove truncate class from detail panel header h2
description: R3-MED-21. The detail panel header shows the node label with CSS truncate class, cutting off long resource names. Nodes in the graph need truncation (fixed NODE_WIDTH=220), but the detail panel header has plenty of room — it should show the full name. Fix: remove the 'truncate' class from the h2 in components/detail-panel/detail-panel.tsx around line 51. Allow the text to wrap instead. Flagged by: UX (MEDIUM).

title: lakebase fixture leaves orphaned external endpoint on CLI 1.1.0
description: During fixture regeneration on Databricks CLI 1.1.0, lakebase-autoscaling repeatedly failed in the after-state deploy while creating resources.postgres_endpoints.external_reader_endpoint on the external prerequisite branch projects/phantom-lakebase/branches/production. Debug run showed POST /api/2.0/postgres/projects/phantom-lakebase/branches/production/endpoints?endpoint_id=dagshund-reader returned 200 with an operation, first operation poll returned 200 done:false, then a later poll returned 404 NOT_FOUND endpoint not found. The endpoint was nevertheless created and appears in list-endpoints, but because the create failed before bundle state recorded it, bundle destroy does not delete it. Direct get/delete can disagree with list/create during the inconsistent state. This blocks a clean lakebase-autoscaling regen even though the plan capture succeeds. Investigate whether this is a Databricks CLI 1.1.0 regression, Lakebase control-plane issue, or fixture design problem; consider avoiding managed resources on external prerequisite branches if the API remains inconsistent.

title: Add underscore prefix to module-internal functions in cli.py
