title: render CLI 1.14 job run outcomes
description:
## Objective

Render Databricks CLI 1.14 `resources.job_runs` semantically in terminal, Markdown, and browser output. The plan action alone is no longer enough: `skip` can mean completed success, a run still in progress, or removal of `on_bundle_deploy`. Preserve the original plan action for counts and detailed exit codes while deriving display semantics from change reasons and remote run state.

## Authoritative CLI 1.14 shapes

Use focused plan vectors based on Databricks CLI v1.14.0. Upstream evidence lives in:

- `acceptance/bundle/resources/job_runs/interrupted_run/output.txt`
- `acceptance/bundle/resources/job_runs/on_bundle_deploy/output.txt`
- `bundle/direct/bundle_plan_test.go`: `TestJobRunFinishedWithoutSuccessIsRecreate`, `TestJobRunInProgressIsSkip`, and `TestJobRunSucceededOutcomeIsNotDrift`

Classify these cases:

1. Completed success: resource action `skip`; remote `result_state` or `state.result_state` is `SUCCESS`; lifecycle is normally `TERMINATED`; `changes.result_state.reason` is normally `remote_already_set`.
2. In progress: resource action `skip`; `changes.result_state.reason == "run in progress"`; remote lifecycle is `PENDING`, `RUNNING`, or `TERMINATING`. CLI 1.14 does not start another run and does not resume waiting for the existing run.
3. Trigger removed: resource action `skip`; a change at `lifecycle`, `lifecycle.triggers`, or `lifecycle.triggers.on_bundle_deploy` has reason `trigger removed`. No run starts.
4. Failed completed run: resource action `recreate`; remote result is `FAILED`, `CANCELED`, or `TIMEDOUT`, or lifecycle is `SKIPPED` or `INTERNAL_ERROR` when no result exists. `remote_state.state.state_message` may explain the outcome. The next deploy re-runs it.
5. Armed every-deploy trigger: resource action `recreate`; lifecycle trigger changes contain non-empty old and new opaque fingerprints under `on_bundle_deploy`. The fingerprints are generated implementation details and must not render.
6. Existing create, ordinary recreate, delete, and older skip shapes remain supported. An unrecognized skip remains the backward-compatible `already ran` fallback.

Extract result state from `remote_state.result_state` first, then `remote_state.state.result_state`. Extract lifecycle and message from `remote_state.state.life_cycle_state` and `remote_state.state.state_message` using safe unknown-value narrowing.

## Required user-facing semantics

Use these exact base phrases:

- create: `runs on deploy`
- ordinary recreate: `re-runs on deploy`
- armed trigger recreate: `runs on every deploy`
- completed-success skip: `already ran successfully`
- unrecognized legacy skip: `already ran`
- in-progress skip: `run still in progress`
- trigger-removal skip: `deploy trigger removed; no run will start`
- delete: `run record will be deleted`

When a recreate has an unsuccessful remote outcome, append `; previous run <OUTCOME>` to either recreate phrase. This also applies when an every-deploy trigger and a failed outcome coexist. Render a non-empty run-level state message as a separate subordinate line/card for in-progress or unsuccessful outcomes. Do not claim task-level detail because plan JSON only carries the run-level message.

Suppress generic field rendering for `result_state`, because it is represented by the semantic outcome and must not be mislabeled as drift. Suppress generated `on_bundle_deploy` fingerprint changes at the three supported lifecycle paths. Only suppress aggregate `lifecycle` or `lifecycle.triggers` entries when their payload is solely the trigger fingerprint container; preserve unrelated lifecycle changes. Preserve all real parameter and configuration changes.

Preserve valid run-page links in Markdown and browser details. Terminal output has never rendered run URLs; do not add terminal URL output in this bead.

## Implementation boundaries

Implement one pure semantic classifier per language and reuse it from every renderer. Do not duplicate condition ladders in terminal, Markdown, badge, and detail components.

Python:

- Extend `JobRunEffect` in `src/dagshund/model.py` with the state needed for classification, preferably `new_state` and `remote_state` to mirror TypeScript.
- Populate those fields in `src/dagshund/merge.py`; do not change target resolution, URL validation, effect ordering, or orphan behavior.
- Put classification and effect-specific visible-change filtering in a focused pure module such as `src/dagshund/job_run_effects.py`.
- Make `src/dagshund/terminal.py` and `src/dagshund/markdown.py` consume the classifier. Keep generic resource field and drift logic unchanged.

TypeScript:

- Keep `normalizePlan` responsible for folding effects and preserving raw state.
- Move action-only wording out of `js/src/utils/normalize-plan.ts` into a focused pure module such as `js/src/utils/job-run-effects.ts`, alongside classification, descriptions, and effect-specific visible-change filtering.
- Use `getUnknownProp` for state inspection. Do not tighten the loose plan Zod schema for these remote fields.
- Make `run-effect-badge.tsx` and `detail-panel/run-effects-section.tsx` consume the shared classifier.

Browser badge policy:

- Exclude delete and trigger-removal effects from the visible badge count.
- If any visible effect fires on deploy, keep the existing green play badge.
- Otherwise, if any visible effect is in progress, render one distinct non-play activity badge using existing palette utilities/styles, with the semantic tooltip.
- Otherwise retain the existing grey completed play badge.
- Keep the tooltip descriptions for all effects when a badge is present. Do not change node diff state.

## Do not implement this elsewhere

This is effect annotation work, not graph topology work. Do not change:

- lateral edge specs, reference specs, resource-key registries, task references, or phantom-node rules
- `build-plan-graph.ts` or `build-resource-graph.ts` effect propagation unless a failing focused test proves an existing propagation bug
- generic `action_config`, generic field-action derivation, structural-diff/drift classification, resource warnings, or resource diff states
- effect target resolution or orphan target behavior
- resource/effect counts, `detect_changes`, dangerous-action classification, or detailed-exit algorithms
- dependencies or the plan schema

The target job must remain unchanged even when a run fires. Effects remain excluded from browser tab counts and diff filters.

## Tests and fixtures

Add `fixtures/job-run-outcome-cases.json` as shared, minimal, hand-authored plan vectors for:

- completed success skip
- in-progress skip
- trigger-removal skip
- failed recreate with state message and run link
- every-deploy recreate with aggregate and leaf fingerprint churn
- every-deploy recreate plus a real parameter change, proving only fingerprint noise is hidden

Test the shared vectors in focused Python and TypeScript classifier tests. Add renderer/component assertions in:

- `tests/test_terminal.py`
- `tests/test_markdown.py`
- `tests/test_cli.py`
- `js/tests/components/run-effect-badge.test.tsx`
- `js/tests/components/detail-panel/run-effects-section.test.tsx`

Acceptance assertions:

- completed, in-progress, and trigger-removal skips are visibly distinct
- trigger removal has no play badge
- in-progress has a distinct activity badge
- failed outcome and useful state message render without a drift label
- generated fingerprints never render, while real parameter changes still do
- safe run links remain in Markdown/browser; unsafe URL rejection remains unchanged
- completed/in-progress/trigger-removal-only plans have detailed exit 0
- failed/every-deploy recreate-only plans have detailed exit 2
- resource and run summary counts remain action-based and unchanged
- parent job diff state and browser tab/filter counts remain unchanged

Do not create a new stateful or supervised golden workflow and do not modify `fixtures/golden/job-runs/before` or `after` to manufacture these states. The existing real `job-runs` golden remains integration evidence for create, ordinary recreate, delete, completed-success skip, links, counts, and effect-only exit 2. If its expected generated output changes because completed-success wording improves, regenerate with `nix develop --command just gen-expected job-runs`; never hand-edit generated golden output. Update README job-run wording to match the final semantics.
close_reason: Implemented semantic CLI 1.14 job run outcomes across terminal, Markdown, and browser with focused cross-language coverage.

title: Build graph model: Plan to React Flow nodes and edges
description:
Transform a parsed Plan (from parser/) into React Flow-compatible nodes and edges. All pure functions, no React code.

WHAT EXISTS:
- Plan type with record of PlanEntry (keyed by resource path string like 'resources.jobs.etl_pipeline')
- Each PlanEntry has: id, depends_on, action, changes, new_state, remote_state
- DiffState type: added | removed | modified | unchanged
- mapActionToDiffState function in parser/map-diff-state.ts
- Two real fixtures: sample-plan.json (all creates) and mixed-plan.json (updates/skips/removals)

KEY INSIGHT — THE DATA HAS THREE LEVELS:
1. Resource level: top-level plan entries keyed like 'resources.jobs.etl_pipeline'. Each has an action (create/update/delete/skip).
2. Task level: inside new_state.value.tasks, each task has task_key, depends_on (array of {task_key}), notebook_task, etc. These form the actual DAG the user wants to see.
3. Change level: the 'changes' record has keys like 'tasks[task_key=extract].notebook_task.notebook_path' with per-field actions (update/skip/delete). This tells us WHICH tasks and fields changed.

THE GRAPH MODEL MUST:
- Extract tasks from new_state.value.tasks as individual graph nodes
- Build edges from each task's depends_on array (task_key references)
- Determine each task's DiffState by checking the changes record:
  - If changes has 'tasks[task_key=X]' with action=update and only a 'new' field (no 'old') → added
  - If changes has 'tasks[task_key=X]' with action=update and only an 'old' field (no 'new') → removed
  - If changes has 'tasks[task_key=X].some.field' with action=update → modified
  - If all changes for task X are action=skip → unchanged
  - If the resource-level action is 'create' → all tasks are added
- Also produce a job-level metadata node showing the resource itself (name, triggers, etc.) — this is context, not part of the task DAG edges
- Handle multiple jobs in the plan (each is a separate sub-graph)

WHAT TO BUILD in src/graph/:
1. Graph types in src/types/graph-types.ts:

title: Click task → slide-in detail panel showing changes
description:
When a user clicks a task node, a detail panel slides in from the right side showing all changes for that task.

### Behavior
- Click a task node → panel slides in from the right (~350-400px wide)
- Panel shows: task name, diff state badge, and a list of all changes
- Each change entry shows: field path, old value, new value, action type
- Click outside panel or click an X button → panel closes
- Clicking a different task updates the panel contents
- Clicking a job container node could show job-level changes

### Data
The `changes` field is already computed and attached to each node's data (`DagNodeData.changes`). It's a `Record<string, ChangeDesc>` where ChangeDesc has old/new values and action.

### Files to create/modify
- `src/components/detail-panel.tsx` — new component for the slide-in panel
- `src/App.tsx` — add state for selected node, render panel conditionally
- `src/hooks/use-selected-node.ts` — optional hook to manage selection state
- `src/components/index.ts` — barrel export

### Styling
Dark theme consistent with existing zinc-950 background. Panel should have a subtle border-left separator. Changes displayed in a clean diff-like format.

title: Filter unchanged and wheel-only changes out of plan review
description:
Large PR plan outputs are dominated by unchanged resources and repeated routine wheel artifact updates. Reviewers need a focused non-wheel change view in terminal, Markdown CI output, and generated HTML, including nested jobs and pipelines, without losing awareness of which wheels are being deployed.

Agreed behavior: wheel suppression changes the effective diff consistently throughout the hierarchy, rather than merely hiding task fields or changing task styling. Wheel-only items become effectively unchanged while suppression is enabled. Mixed items retain their non-wheel differences. Wheel information is summarized separately once per plan, rather than repeated per task or job. Original plan data remains available for the full unsuppressed view.

Reuse existing controls: --suppress-wheel-updates and the HTML wheel-suppression toggle, combined with existing status/unchanged filters. No new combined filter or CLI flags are needed. The intended CI command is dagshund plan.json -c --suppress-wheel-updates; -c already aliases --changes-only.
design:
Agreed presentation and filtering contract

1. Suppression off: preserve existing full diff behavior. Wheel-only resources count as modified, and wheel differences appear inline. Existing status filters continue to work normally.
2. Suppression on: routine wheel churn does not contribute to effective change classification. Apply this consistently to tasks, resources, parent jobs and other containers, including supported nested job and pipeline shapes. A parent must not remain modified solely because of suppressed descendant wheel changes; its own substantive differences and substantive descendant differences still count.
3. Every presentation uses the same effective diff: node styling, badges, summary/filter counts, status filtering, detail-panel differences, changed-task lists, and terminal/Markdown resource sections. Do not leave suppressed task changes listed as changes in parent details.
4. Existing -c/--changes-only, -m/--modified, and -f status:modified must use the wheel-suppressed classification when suppression is enabled. With suppression alone, wheel-only items may remain visible as unchanged. With suppression plus changes-only, unchanged and wheel-only items are excluded from review results. Any HTML ancestors retained solely for navigation are neutral context, not reported changes.
5. Preserve real additions/removals, genuine drift, topology changes, and substantive dependency/resource differences. Suppression must not conceal resource/task creation or deletion just because wheels are involved. Verify the precise routine-churn boundary against representative real shapes; wheel additions/removals, distribution swaps, extras changes, and meaningful compatibility changes are not routine rebuild noise.

Separate wheel summary

Replace per-job wheel-updated lines with one plan-level Wheel updates section while suppression is enabled, consistently in terminal, Markdown, and HTML. Suppress repetition, not information that wheels changed. Each distinct distribution plus old/new version transition appears once; different transitions for the same distribution remain separate. Show accurate affected-carrier/resource counts where appropriate, without labeling pipeline/environment carriers as tasks. Account for supported same-version artifact-path updates without inventing a version transition.

The wheel summary survives changes-only filtering, including updates belonging to wheel-only resources that no longer appear in individual review sections. It is separate from non-wheel change counts and must not make those resources count as modified. Exact formatting and interaction details may follow existing output conventions; no new control is required. Behavior with additional explicit search/type filters should be made coherent during implementation.

Output examples, schematic rather than a formatting redesign:
- Mixed plan: show the actual non-wheel resource differences, a non-wheel change count, then Wheel updates listing each distinct transition once across affected jobs/tasks.
- Only wheel updates: No non-wheel changes, followed by Wheel updates. Do not claim No changes or omit the wheel information.
- Truly unchanged plan: No changes, with no empty wheel section.

HTML uses the same semantics: a plan-level wheel summary, effective status/filter/count/detail behavior, and full original differences restored when suppression is switched off. Disabling CLI suppression restores ordinary full wheel diffs on the next invocation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Suppression consistently treats wheel-only items and their otherwise unchanged parent containers as effectively unchanged in HTML, Markdown, and terminal output.
- [x] Mixed resources retain every non-wheel difference, while genuine additions/removals, drift, topology changes, and substantive dependency changes remain reviewable.
- [x] Existing status controls (-c, -m, -f status:modified, and HTML unchanged/status filtering) consume the effective classification; suppression plus changes-only removes unchanged/wheel-only review noise without a new filter or flag.
- [x] Styles, badges, summary/filter counts, parent detail panels, and changed-task lists agree; no suppressed wheel-only task remains listed as a substantive parent change.
- [x] Suppression produces a separate deduplicated plan-level wheel summary instead of per-job wheel-updated lines. Distinct transitions remain distinguishable and affected-carrier counts are accurate.
- [x] The wheel summary remains visible with changes-only even when all individual wheel-only resources are filtered out. Wheel-only plans say No non-wheel changes and still report wheel updates; truly unchanged plans say No changes.
- [x] Suppression off preserves/restores full original differences and statuses; HTML retains the full plan for reversible toggling.
- [x] Representative regression cases cover nested jobs, pipelines, classic/serverless carriers, wheel-only and mixed changes, parent propagation, filters/counts/details, and the genuine-change boundary across Python and TypeScript behavior.
- [x] Any private user fixture used for investigation remains out of Git; committed regression cases must be independently safe/sanitized.
notes: Behavior agreed with the user in discussion. Current implementation suppresses task fields/styles but leaves parent jobs modified and parent detail lists noisy; terminal/Markdown report classification also remains based on unsuppressed actions. The original per-job wheel-updated line was a summarization workaround, not a requirement to retain that placement. The user still wants awareness of wheel deployment, so the agreed replacement is a separate plan-level wheel summary, not silent removal. A private fixture may be supplied later; do not request or use it yet, and never commit it. This update records the agreement only; implementation has not started.

title: Implement: Shared effective wheel diff and plan summary semantics
description:
## Outcome
Implement a shared, pure presentation policy in Python and TypeScript that removes routine wheel transitions from the effective diff and produces one plan-wide summary. This is the prerequisite for report and browser consumers, not a second normalization system. Parent dagshund-eicp and approval comment 492 define scope. No new dependencies, flags, raw-plan mutation, deployment behavior changes, or private fixtures.

## Existing path and exact sites
Python: src/dagshund/wheel.py (classify_wheel_update, collect_wheel_updates, summarize_wheel_updates, WheelUpdate/Usage), model.py (ResourceChange/FieldChange, compare_field_values, UNSET), merge.py normalize_plan, plan.py classify_resource_drift/is_topology_drift_change/action_to_diff_state. TypeScript: js/src/utils/wheel-updates.ts, normalize-plan.ts (NormalizedPlan/NormalizedEntry), structural-diff.ts, deep-equal.ts; graph/resolve-task-diff-state.ts and utils/task-key.ts define task change ownership. Existing mirrored classifiers only recognize tasks[task_key='K'].libraries[N].whl, optional for_each_task.task, and environments[environment_key='K'].spec.dependencies[N]. They deduplicate by versions, losing distinct same-version path transitions. Existing shared fixture fixtures/wheel-update-cases.json is loaded by tests/test_wheel.py and js/tests/utils/wheel-updates.test.ts.

## Chosen interfaces and ordering
1. Extend the narrow carrier classifier with resource-type context, not arbitrary recursive scanning for .whl strings. Retain current same-distribution/same-extras policy including same-version path updates. In jobs accept the existing paths. In pipelines also accept libraries[N].whl and environment.dependencies[N]. The installed declared Databricks CLI's auth-free `databricks bundle schema` confirms pipelines.PipelineLibrary.whl and pipelines.PipelinesEnvironment.dependencies, including classic/serverless pipeline environments. Do not accidentally make job-level libraries[N].whl valid. Whole-array or keyed-library replacements are not proven routine scalar transitions and remain substantive.
2. Add pure apply_wheel_suppression(resources) in Python and applyWheelSuppression(normalizedPlan) in TypeScript. Inputs are already normalized. Return effective resources/NormalizedPlan plus sorted wheel summary usages. Preserve mapping keys as authoritative identities. Consumers call this only for suppression; the original normalized plan remains available for off mode. Use immutable copies only where needed; retain state wrappers, current/remote values, dependencies, run effects and orphan effects unchanged. Do not change normalization, Plan.raw, browser PlanContext, or parser schemas.
3. Suppress only proven update transitions in update resources. Never downgrade create/delete/recreate/resize/update_id/unknown resources or hide whole task additions/removals/topology re-adds. Retain every non-wheel substantive change, drift, unknown evidence, and merged-subresource change. Unknown or incomplete data is not evidence of a wheel-only entry. Do not infer changes along run_job_task or pipeline_task reference edges: those are relationships, not owned subresources.
4. In an affected entry, derive effective changes by removing eligible wheel scalar changes. Proven no-op entries may be excluded from the effective projection to prevent no-op action labels retaining modified task/parent states: old/new equal with remote present and equal is a no-op; old==new without remote can be topology drift and must remain. Preserve other fields, including skip/empty entries where their data are still needed; they must not count as substantive unless existing drift/topology semantics say otherwise. If at least one wheel transition was suppressed and no substantive changes remain, replace only the presentation action update with skip. Mixed entries stay update. Do not turn an update with missing/empty changes into unchanged just because no visible fields exist. The resulting changes must let existing task diff resolution, job task summaries, resource badges and derived-owner states all agree without a second task-only display override. If a narrow adjustment to resolveTaskDiffState is needed for neutral remaining keys, keep it limited to effective-view semantics and test off-mode compatibility.
5. Summary identity is the exact (distribution, old wheel requirement, new wheel requirement), including full paths and extras, not just versions; this preserves distinct artifact transitions with identical versions. Keep parsed versions for display. Deduplicate occurrences using resource key + carrier kind + carrier identity, never task/environment name alone or library slot index. Task identity includes the optional for_each inner-task scope. Job environments count once per environment, not per task referring to it. Pipeline libraries count once per pipeline, and pipeline environment dependencies once per pipeline environment. Return task/environment/pipeline carrier counts explicitly; a repeated transition on one carrier counts once, while carriers in different resources count separately. Sort deterministically by distribution then old/new requirement. Expose a shared formatting contract: versions identify normal transitions; include old/new requirement text when versions alone are ambiguous or equal so distinct summaries are visibly distinguishable. Renderers escape that text at their normal boundaries.

## Tests and verification
Extend fixtures/wheel-update-cases.json without invalidating its current negative job-library case; add resource type to pipeline vectors. Add fixtures/wheel-suppression-cases.json with small synthetic normalized-input expectations and complete representative raw plans for downstream consumers. Include nested for_each and managed run-job/pipeline references without changing graph topology, mixed permissions, drift, run effects, repeated transitions across resources and all negative boundaries in acceptance criteria. Reuse tests/factories.py and JS parse/normalize helpers. Add tests/test_wheel_suppression.py and js/tests/utils/wheel-suppression.test.ts if separate pure projection modules are clearer; concrete consumers are the next two implementation beads.
Run through `direnv exec /home/chinchy/projects/dagshund`: `uv run pytest -q tests/test_wheel.py tests/test_wheel_suppression.py`; `bun test --cwd js tests/utils/wheel-updates.test.ts tests/utils/wheel-suppression.test.ts`; `just typecheck`. Follow the Python, TypeScript and testing guidelines. Do not run authenticated fixture regeneration.
acceptance_criteria: Python and TypeScript consume the same independently authored safe vectors and agree on effective entry actions/remaining changes and sorted wheel summaries. Cover classic tasks, for_each inner-task carriers, job environments, pipeline libraries and pipeline environment dependencies; wheel-only and mixed entries; normalized permission subresources; run-job/pipeline references; same carrier names in different resources; repeated slots on one carrier; distinct artifact transitions with identical versions; and no mutation. Negative cases preserve resource/task adds/removes, recreate/resize/update_id/unknown actions, drift and topology re-adds, ordinary dependency changes, extras changes, different distributions, malformed wheels, missing values, and unrelated wheel-looking fields. Suppression off preserves the original normalized data and all raw snapshots/effects. Focused Python/Bun tests and both typechecks pass.

title: Implement: Effective terminal and Markdown wheel review
description:
## Outcome and prerequisite
Consume dagshund-eicp.1's effective wheel projection in terminal/Markdown report preparation. This bead owns Python report/UI plumbing and CLI-help wording, not the core classifier or HTML implementation. The user-facing command is `dagshund plan.json -c --suppress-wheel-updates`; -c already means changes-only. No new filter or flag. Follow Python/testing guidelines.

## Existing entry points
src/dagshund/cli.py: _run normalizes once, _render_stdout forwards suppress_wheel_updates to both renderers, _build_visible_states builds -c/-m states. Detailed exit codes use unsuppressed normalized resources in _run; retain this behavior.
src/dagshund/format.py: prepare_report -> filter_resources/iter_visible_resources -> count_by_action -> Report; select_resource_details currently suppresses fields and returns per-resource wheel_updates; format_wheel_update_body is shared by output renderers. filter.py build_query_predicate currently uses entry.action for status filters. terminal.py render_text and markdown.py render_markdown currently call prepare_report before suppression, return early on report.no_changes, and emit wheel lines from each resource. Existing tests: tests/test_format.py, test_filter.py, test_terminal.py, test_markdown.py, test_cli.py. Existing wheel golden: fixtures/golden/wheel-bump/plan.json and expected-suppressed.txt/.md.

## Implementation steps
1. Add suppression to prepare_report and use the shared pure effective resource mapping BEFORE visible-state/query filtering, groups, action counts and detail selection. Keep original inputs intact. Supply plan-wide wheel usages on Report, computed before any visibility filtering. The summary describes the plan, not just selected resources, even for -m or a type/name/field query. Reuse existing filter semantics on the effective entries rather than introducing a second status predicate.
2. Preserve the distinction between source-plan change detection and effective non-wheel change detection. `No non-wheel changes` applies when suppression actually removed wheel changes and no non-wheel deploy changes remain across the plan, not merely when a user filter matches nothing. `No changes` remains the message for genuinely unchanged plans. Keep existing job-run effects/standalone run behavior: pending runs are real non-wheel activity and must not be mislabeled a wheel-only no-op. Visibility filters must not alter global emptiness truth.
3. Move wheel usage rendering into one separate top-level Wheel updates section in each output; remove per-job/per-resource wheel-updated lines and their obsolete ResourceDetails plumbing. The section must render even if groups are empty or the no-non-wheel message is taken. Use dagshund-eicp.1's summary identity/counts; normal version transitions remain compact, same-version/ambiguous transitions expose exact old/new requirements so entries remain distinguishable. Reuse terminal control-character escaping and Markdown plain-text/code escaping. Do not leak raw unescaped paths into either output.
4. A wheel-only resource appears unchanged with suppression when ordinary resource groups are shown; mixed resources keep non-wheel details. Warnings and drift summaries must remain intact for genuine changes. Off mode is the existing full report with no new wheel summary. Preserve --detailed-exitcode, --quiet, browser payload generation, and source provenance semantics. Suppression is a review projection, not a claim that deployment has no changes.
5. Update cli.py usage example/help from once-per-job wording to a plan-level summary and the -c combination. No README/browser wording here: final integration owns combined documentation to avoid parallel edits.

## Verification
Add table-driven direct-renderer and CLI tests using safe vectors from fixtures/wheel-suppression-cases.json. Assert full unfiltered vs suppressed, -c/-m/status:modified/status:unchanged, wheel-only/no-change/mixed plans, duplicate task/environment names across jobs, pipeline carriers, same-version distinct transitions, nested for_each, merged permissions, genuine additions/removals and drift, and unchanged detailed exit codes. Existing tests assert old per-job behavior; update only intended assertions.
Run all commands via `direnv exec /home/chinchy/projects/dagshund`: `uv run pytest -q tests/test_format.py tests/test_filter.py tests/test_terminal.py tests/test_markdown.py tests/test_cli.py`; `just typecheck-py`; `just gen-expected wheel-bump`; `just test-golden`. Load the update-fixtures skill before maintaining generated expectations. Regenerate local expected output only using its generator, never hand-edit generated files or deploy/regenerate Databricks plans. Inspect the golden diff and require unsuppressed outputs/exit-code expectations to remain unchanged. If another existing suppressed golden legitimately changes, regenerate only that affected fixture and explain why.
acceptance_criteria: Both renderers and CLI show effective actions/counts/details with suppression enabled. -c, -m, and -f status:modified exclude wheel-only resources; status:unchanged includes them when the report otherwise renders resource groups. A single plan-wide wheel summary survives all resource visibility filters with accurate deduplicated counts and distinguishable transitions. Wheel-only plans say No non-wheel changes and list wheels; truly unchanged plans retain No changes; mixed plans retain non-wheel fields, drift and safety warnings. Off-mode output and detailed exit codes remain unchanged. Tests cover direct renderer APIs and CLI term/md paths with safe nested-job/pipeline fixtures; regenerated suppressed golden expectations and focused tests pass.

title: Implement: Reversible effective wheel review across HTML views
description:
## Outcome and prerequisite
Consume dagshund-eicp.1's immutable effective NormalizedPlan and plan-wide wheel usages for HTML, replacing the current task-only styling workaround. Keep the existing Hide wheel updates control, default off, but make its state plan-scoped across Jobs/Resources views. No new toggle, flag, dependency, graph topology feature, or raw-plan rewriting. Follow TypeScript, visualization and testing guidelines.

## Current data path and exact change sites
js/src/app.tsx PlanView owns parsed Plan -> normalizePlan -> preparePlan, mounts both tabs, and puts the original parsed/redacted Plan in PlanContext. hooks/use-plan-graph.ts and use-resource-graph.ts build/layout PreparedPlan. components/resources-view.tsx and app.tsx DagView pass data into FlowCanvas.
components/flow-canvas.tsx currently owns hideWheelUpdates in canvasReducer separately per tab, derives wheelUpdateCount only from job nodes, uses resolveDisplayedDiffState for filter counts but stores selected data snapshots. flow-canvas-layout.tsx renders the existing toggle with per-job tooltip. hooks/contexts.ts InteractionContext and components/task-node.tsx/utils/node-data.ts provide the task-only display override. components/job-node.tsx shows a per-job wheel badge.
graph/build-plan-graph.ts builds wheelUpdates/isWheelOnlyChange metadata; graph/build-resource-nodes.ts buildJobFields creates job status and buildTaskChangeSummary from original entry.changes, and buildDerivedNode inherits owner action. graph/build-task-change-summary.ts and resolve-task-diff-state.ts handle task lists. types/graph-types.ts defines obsolete wheel-specific per-node fields. components/detail-panel/detail-panel.tsx reads data.diffState/data.changes/taskChangeSummary; its raw JSON disclosure uses original PlanContext via extract-raw-plan-entry.ts. hooks/use-node-search.ts and utils/node-search-text.ts read ordinary graph data for status matching.

## Chosen integration
1. Lift only wheel-suppression state to PlanView; leave other canvas filters/interactions local. Derive original normalized plan once; when suppression is on, feed dagshund-eicp.1's effective normalized view into preparePlan and both graph hooks. Keep PlanContext pointing to original parsed Plan so raw/history inspection and off-mode reconstruction are exact. Do not mutate prepared projections or patch DOM styles as a substitute for effective graph data.
2. Pass the shared wheel-toggle state/callback and plan-wide transition count down to both FlowCanvas instances using typed props (through DagView and ResourcesView). Preserve initial off behavior; the CLI output flags still do not destructively prefilter HTML or change its initial controls. Toggle availability must work with pipeline-only plans and in Resources, not rely on JobGraphNode metadata.
3. With effective actions/changes upstream, normal graph builders must produce consistent task/job/resource/derived-owner data and taskChangeSummary. Remove the obsolete per-task isWheelOnlyChange override, per-job wheelUpdates badge/summary and duplicate counters/types/context fields that this change orphans. Preserve real node IDs, current snapshots, resource relationships, edge differences, drift flags and run-effect annotations. Do not propagate modified state across arbitrary run-job or pipeline-reference edges.
4. Derive selected detail data by selected node ID from the CURRENT graph nodes instead of retaining stale data captured on click. A toggle while a panel is open must update its badge, fields and changed-task list; toggling off restores them without requiring reselect. Preserve existing hidden-phantom selection behavior and layout-hook cancellation/error handling. Do not add a separate recovery or state ownership layer.
5. Render a single Plan-level Wheel updates summary in PlanView outside both canvases and their visibility/status/search filters, using the full pre-filter summary. Show it only with suppression on and actual routine transitions. Display distribution, old/new versions or disambiguating old/new requirements per the core contract, and explicit task/environment/pipeline carrier counts. Use React text escaping; do not render unsafe HTML. Keep it concise and accessible, allow long paths to wrap. Use a bounded scroll area if necessary so a large summary cannot displace the graph entirely.
6. Show `No non-wheel changes` for a globally wheel-only effective plan while keeping summary and controls accessible, and `No changes` for a genuinely unchanged plan. Do not confuse a filter with zero matches with a globally unchanged plan. Active run effects/orphan effects remain genuine activity. The status-filter behavior remains the existing graph highlight/dimming model, not a new destructive node deletion mode. Tab resource totals retain their existing total-resource meaning; status/filter counts reflect effective classification.

## Tests and verification
Reuse js/tests/helpers/build-graphs-from-plan.ts, providers.tsx and xyflow-mock.ts. Extend graph/build-plan-graph.test.ts, build-resource-graph.test.ts, build-task-change-summary.test.ts, components/flow-canvas.test.tsx, job-node/task-node tests, and app.test.tsx; add focused plan-summary/detail tests as needed. Load core safe shared vectors with actual normalize -> suppression -> prepare -> public graph paths, not duplicated test-only classification. Cover nested for_each, nested managed run-job/pipeline references, mixed/wheel-only jobs and pipelines in both tabs, derived outputs inheriting effective owner action, duplicated carrier names, summary independence from filters, on/off/on with a selected parent/task, status:modified search plus toolbar counts, drift/topology/add/remove/extras/PyPI boundaries, and original raw JSON.
Run via `direnv exec /home/chinchy/projects/dagshund`: `bun test --cwd js tests/graph/build-plan-graph.test.ts tests/graph/build-resource-graph.test.ts tests/graph/build-task-change-summary.test.ts tests/components/flow-canvas.test.tsx tests/app.test.tsx`; `just test-js`; `just typecheck-js`; `bun run --cwd js build:template`. Generated packaged assets must come from js/scripts/build-template.ts, never manual editing. Final integration owns README/screenshot consistency and cross-format manual verification.
acceptance_criteria: In both Jobs and Resources tabs, one shared existing wheel toggle changes effective job/task/pipeline/derived-owner statuses, styles, status search/filter matches and counts, detail badges/fields and changed-task lists consistently. No wheel-only task remains a substantive parent change. One plan-level wheel summary with accurate deduplicated carriers remains visible regardless of graph status filters or selected tab, including pipeline-only/no-job plans. Wheel-only plans show No non-wheel changes; truly unchanged plans show No changes without fabricated wheel entries. Switching on/off while a detail is open refreshes the same node's details and restores original full differences, while raw JSON remains original. Topology, references, drift, additions/removals, effects and non-wheel changes survive. Pure graph and React integration tests, TypeScript typecheck, and generated-template build pass.
close_reason: Accepted summary-row/nonzero-count correction integrated at 7339290ff5a2aef411b2c700ad93abd5bce50345 with clean final-H3 build/check/supported-Python gates. Canonical evidence 580, UI receipt 581; task review closed. Final combined/result acceptance remains pending.

Keep actual browser inspection separate from mocked-library evidence. title: Python package wrapper for PyPI/uvx distribution
description:
Create a Python package that bundles pre-built JS/CSS assets and provides a CLI entry point, enabling installation via uvx dagshund or pip install dagshund. No Node/Bun runtime needed on the user's machine.

Target UX:
  databricks bundle plan -o json | uvx dagshund
  uvx dagshund plan.json
  uvx dagshund plan.json -o report.html

Architecture:
- Python package with zero dependencies (just string templating + webbrowser)
- Pre-built HTML template with placeholder for plan JSON injection
- CLI reads plan from stdin or file arg, injects into template, opens browser
- Package structure: pyproject.toml + src/dagshund/{__init__.py, cli.py, _assets/template.html}
- Build pipeline: bun run build -> assemble template HTML with placeholder -> commit into _assets/
- ~2.5MB package size (bundled JS)

Requires further evaluation:
- Template generation script (similar to cli.ts but outputs placeholder instead of real plan)
- PyPI publishing workflow (CI/CD for build + publish)
- Whether to keep the dev server mode (Python HTTP server) or export-only
- Version sync between TS and Python package
- Whether to add optional plan validation in Python (via json schema) or rely on JS-side Zod
notes: Requires further evaluation before implementation. See conversation for full design discussion.

title: audit CLI 1.14.0 compatibility and schema edges
description:
## Context

Dagshund is last validated against Databricks CLI 1.10.0. Audit the upstream v1.11.0, v1.12.0, and v1.12.1 release changes and regenerate against the latest release, currently v1.12.1.

Upstream audit identified no core plan parser incompatibility. Dagshund accepts unknown resource types, fields, and actions through its loose Python and TypeScript plan models. The following user-facing behavior and fixture coverage still need investigation or implementation.

## CLI 1.12.1 refresh

- Regenerate the bundle schema and all eligible golden fixtures against Databricks CLI 1.14.0 using the update-fixtures skill.
- Regenerate supervised manual drift and inspect every substantive plan/output change before blessing.
- Keep the classic-compute wheel-bump exception from the fixture workflow.
- Update README validation text and audit affected screenshots.
- Verify the SDK v0.170.0-only v1.12.1 patch does not change emitted bundle plan shapes.

## Job run outcomes, CLI 1.12.0

PR: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6091

The experimental job_runs resource now waits for completion and compares a desired result_state of SUCCESS with remote run state.

Observed plan shapes:
- An interrupted, still-running run uses resource action update and field reason \"run in progress\".
- A failed, canceled, timed-out, or skipped run uses resource action recreate.
- new_state.value.result_state is SUCCESS.
- remote_state can carry result_state, state.life_cycle_state, state.state_message, run_id, and run_page_url.

Dagshund currently folds job_runs onto jobs, but update falls back to generic wording and the badge treats it like an already-completed run. Result state and state message are not surfaced clearly.

Required work:
- Add accurate in-progress and outcome wording in terminal, Markdown, and browser views.
- Distinguish running/adopted runs from already-ran skip effects in badges.
- Surface useful failed/result state without exposing irrelevant raw noise.
- Extend the job-runs fixture for update, recreate, running, success, and failed result shapes.
- Verify detailed exit codes and counts remain correct for effect-only update and recreate plans.

Idempotency tokens are managed entirely by the CLI and require no Dagshund behavior.

## Unity Catalog secrets, CLI 1.12.0

PR: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/5861

The new resource key is resources.secrets, distinct from resources.secret_scopes. Plan state includes catalog_name, schema_name, name, comment, and redacted value/effective_value fields.

Required work:
- Add create, update, recreate, delete, grants, and redacted-value fixture coverage where supported.
- Place secrets as leaves beneath their Unity Catalog catalog/schema rather than as generic workspace resources.
- Add an appropriate resource badge and naming behavior.
- Keep secret_scopes behavior separate from UC secrets.
- Verify no secret value can leak through terminal, Markdown, browser detail, raw JSON, screenshots, or test output. Upstream should redact values, but Dagshund must validate this boundary.
- Decide whether secret deletion should receive a destructive credential-loss warning.

## Pipeline cascade deletion, CLI 1.12.0

PR: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/5846

pipelines.cascade_on_destroy controls whether destroying a pipeline also deletes its managed materialized views, streaming tables, and views. False retains datasets; true deletes them; unset uses the backend default, which cascades. Changing only this field is a state-only update.

Required work:
- Add fixture coverage for false, true, unset, state-only update, and pipeline deletion.
- Warn accurately about managed dataset loss on destructive pipeline plans.
- Determine whether plan JSON contains enough persisted-state information to make the warning conditional. If not, use conservative wording rather than claiming datasets will definitely be deleted.

## Release-change regression fixtures

Add or extend focused coverage for relevant upstream fixes even where no production-code change is currently expected:

- Empty grants migration and revocation behavior: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6039
- Job/task/for_each webhook ordering convergence: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6060
- Pipeline allow_duplicate_names convergence: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6076
- Input-only fields no longer being silently omitted: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6112
- Postgres sensitive-field redaction revert and duration drift: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6179
- Model-serving telemetry_config drift and updates: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6106
- AI Runtime task local code_source_path packaging and workspace-path rewrite: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6110
- Vector Search recreate while the old index name is pending deletion: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6143. This is deployment timing behavior, but preserve representative recreate rendering if practical.

## Bundle-schema relationship audit

The generated Databricks bundle schema contains reference-bearing fields not currently represented as Dagshund graph edges. For every candidate below, first produce a real direct-engine plan fixture and inspect the emitted new_state and remote_state shape. Implement only relationships supported by actual plan evidence.

### Known candidates

1. Vector Search index to Vector Search endpoint
   - Source resource: vector_search_indexes
   - Schema field: endpoint_name
   - Expected target: vector_search_endpoints
   - This is the clearest missing relationship and should be prioritized.

2. Cluster to instance pools
   - Source resource: clusters, including job clusters where applicable
   - Schema fields: instance_pool_id and driver_instance_pool_id
   - Expected target: instance_pools
   - Resolve both bundle interpolation references and deployed API IDs.

3. Postgres role membership
   - Source resource: postgres_roles
   - Schema field: membership_roles
   - Expected targets: other postgres_roles
   - Determine direction and whether these are hierarchy or lateral edges.

4. Quality monitor to output schema
   - Source resource: quality_monitors
   - Schema field: output_schema_name
   - Expected target: schemas or a schema phantom.

5. Pipeline event log to Unity Catalog hierarchy
   - Source resource: pipelines
   - Schema field: event_log and its catalog/schema destination fields
   - Expected targets: catalogs/schemas, based on actual emitted state.

6. UC secret to catalog/schema
   - Source resource: secrets
   - Schema fields: catalog_name and schema_name
   - Expected hierarchy placement beneath the matching schema.

### Full audit method

- Compare every resource and nested resource definition in the CLI 1.12.1 generated bundle schema against Dagshund registries and extractors in resource-key.ts, reference-specs.ts, extract-lateral-edges.ts, build-resource-graph.ts, derived-node-specs.ts, and task reference handling.
- Inventory fields that contain resource IDs, names, full names, parent paths, source/target references, warehouse IDs, endpoint names, catalog/schema names, job IDs, pipeline IDs, dashboard IDs, model names, and bundle interpolation strings.
- Classify each as hierarchy, lateral dependency, task dependency, derived output, effect, or intentionally not an edge.
- Avoid duplicate edges already represented through hierarchy or derived-node promotion.
- Document intentional omissions in code or close as no-action with evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- Databricks CLI 1.14.0 schema and eligible goldens are regenerated and reviewed.
- All substantive fixture drift is explained before expected output is blessed.
- job_runs running and failed outcomes are represented accurately across all renderers.
- UC secrets are safely rendered and correctly placed in the resource graph without value leakage.
- Pipeline cascade deletion risk is communicated accurately.
- Every schema reference candidate has either a real fixture and implemented edge or a documented evidence-based no-action decision.
- Python and TypeScript tests cover every implemented behavior.
- Full quality gate and production build pass.
- Browser verification and required screenshots are completed according to the repository workflow.
## CLI 1.13.0 additions

### Job runs on every bundle deploy

PR: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6231

resources.job_runs can now set lifecycle.triggers.on_bundle_deploy: true. The CLI stores a generated fingerprint and recreates the run on every deploy even when bundle configuration is unchanged. Removing the trigger emits an update with reason \"trigger removed\" and performs a state-only update without running the job.

Observed plan behavior:
- Armed trigger: action recreate on every deploy.
- lifecycle and lifecycle.triggers.on_bundle_deploy changes contain generated UUID fingerprints.
- Trigger removal: action update, old lifecycle present, no new lifecycle, and no RunNow call.
- result_state remains a skip when the previous run succeeded.

Required work:
- Extend the job-runs fixture with armed, repeated-deploy, and trigger-removal plans.
- Render an armed trigger semantically as \"runs on every deploy\" rather than exposing generated UUID churn.
- Do not render trigger removal as if a run will execute. It is a state-only effect update.
- Ensure browser badges distinguish run-firing recreate from non-running trigger-removal update.
- Keep effect counts and detailed exit code correct for the state-only update.

### Pip extras on local wheel dependencies

PR: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6291

Serverless job environment dependencies can now contain local wheel paths with an extras suffix, for example foo-1.2.3-py3-none-any.whl[train]. The CLI preserves the suffix when rewriting the wheel to its uploaded workspace path.

Dagshund wheel suppression currently requires dependency strings to end exactly in .whl, so parse_wheel_filename in both Python and TypeScript rejects .whl[extras]. This prevents --suppress-wheel-updates and the browser wheel-update toggle from recognizing otherwise ordinary version bumps.

Required work:
- Parse and validate an optional pip extras suffix after .whl in Python and TypeScript.
- Suppress a version-only wheel update when distribution and extras are unchanged.
- Treat an extras addition, removal, or change as a real dependency change that must remain visible.
- Add shared wheel-update cases for one extra, multiple extras, changed extras, malformed suffixes, and uploaded workspace paths.
- Add a serverless golden fixture case if the 1.13.0 plan exposes this shape.

### Other 1.13.0 release items

No Dagshund production change is currently expected for deploy/destroy action summaries, Git metadata fixes, direct-engine migration sequencing, secret-scope validation, atomic deployment-state writes, newer-CLI state warnings, or SDK/provider/toolchain bumps. Confirm this classification during fixture regeneration.
## CLI 1.14.0 additions and corrections

### Revised job_runs skip semantics

PR: https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6357

CLI 1.14.0 supersedes part of the 1.12.0 and 1.13.0 job_runs behavior recorded above:

- A still-running job run now has resource action skip, not update.
- Its result_state field has action skip, reason \"run in progress\", and new SUCCESS. remote_state.state.life_cycle_state remains RUNNING.
- Removing lifecycle.triggers.on_bundle_deploy now has resource action skip, not update.
- Trigger removal emits a lifecycle field with action skip and reason \"trigger removed\" and does not run the job.
- An armed on_bundle_deploy trigger still emits recreate on every deploy with generated lifecycle UUID fingerprints.
- A failed completed run still emits recreate and should run again.

Required work:
- Treat the CLI 1.14.0 shapes as authoritative when updating the job-runs fixture and implementation.
- Do not count in-progress or trigger-removal skip entries as deploy changes.
- Do not label every skip effect \"already ran\". Distinguish an in-progress run from a completed run using remote_state.state.life_cycle_state and change reason.
- Render trigger removal as unchanged/state cleanup, not as a run that fires.
- Continue collapsing generated on_bundle_deploy UUID fingerprint churn into semantic \"runs on every deploy\" wording.
- Preserve recreate wording and run links for failed completed runs.

### Cluster policies resource and references

PRs:
- https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6225
- https://github.com/databricks/cli/pull/6304

CLI 1.14.0 adds the direct-engine-only resources.cluster_policies resource, including per-resource permissions. Jobs can reference a policy through new_cluster.policy_id, and the CLI records the dependency so policy creation precedes job creation and job deletion precedes policy deletion.

Required work:
- Add cluster policy create, update, delete, permissions, backend-normalization, family, and out-of-band drift fixture coverage as practical.
- Add a cluster policy resource badge and generic detail coverage.
- Add graph relationships from jobs to cluster policies for task new_cluster.policy_id and job_clusters[*].new_cluster.policy_id.
- Audit standalone clusters policy_id references as part of the existing schema-edge candidate work.
- Resolve bundle interpolation references and deployed policy API IDs, producing phantoms for external policies where useful.
- Decide whether task-level policy relationships belong on task nodes, the containing job node, or only the resource graph. Avoid duplicate edges.

### Deeper generated schema fields

CLI 1.14.0 raises the resource schema generator recursion cap from four to ten levels. Regenerate the v1.14.0 bundle schema before completing the relationship audit and rescan newly exposed nested fields for references. Do not assume the v1.10.0 schema inventory was complete.

### Other relevant 1.14.0 fixture validation

- App resource securable_kind no longer creates permanent output-only drift. Validate app-dependencies fixture convergence.
- Removed or externally changed fields on schemas, catalogs, volumes, registered models, and external locations are now sent as cleared rather than producing a plan the deploy does not apply. Regenerate representative update and manual-drift cases and verify Dagshund renders field removal accurately.
- Automatic migration from Terraform to direct can change which engine produces plans, but Dagshund already requires and tests direct-engine plan JSON. Confirm documentation remains accurate.

No Dagshund production change is expected for destroy summary counts, workspace directory cleanup, SSH keepalives, resource wait timeout, or SDK/provider bumps.

description: Fix issues identified during the full codebase review. This sits between the review and CI/CD setup — all findings should be resolved before the pipeline codifies current patterns.

title: refresh Python and JavaScript dependencies
description:
Refresh direct Python and JavaScript dependencies after the Bun 1.4.0 upgrade. Dagshund has no Python runtime dependencies.

Implemented versions:
- Python build/dev: hatchling 1.32.0, prek 0.4.14, pytest 9.1.1, pytest-cov 7.1.0, Ruff 0.16.3, ty 0.0.73.
- JavaScript runtime: @xyflow/react 12.11.5, elkjs 0.12.0, React/react-dom 19.2.8, yaml 2.9.0, Zod 4.4.3.
- JavaScript dev: Biome 2.5.9, happy-dom 20.11.6, Tailwind and CLI 4.3.3, user-event 14.6.6, React types 19.2.18/19.2.5, TypeScript 7.0.2. @types/bun 1.4.0 and testing-library/react 16.3.2 remain current.
- Nixpkgs refreshed from the 2026-07-18 revision to the 2026-08-23 revision, advancing Python to 3.14.7, uv to 0.12.5, and the Nix-provided development tools.
- GitLab CI uv image refreshed from 0.11.7 to digest-pinned 0.12.5.

Intentional registry gaps:
- Nixpkgs currently provides ty 0.0.73, Ruff 0.16.3, and Biome 2.5.9 while registries have 0.0.74, 0.16.4, and 2.5.10. Keep project pins aligned with the actual Nix shell rather than adding custom overrides for one-release gaps.

Compatibility work:
- TypeScript 7.0.2 native compiler passes the strict frontend typecheck without source changes.
- ty 0.0.73 enables the opt-in unsound-return-statement rule through all = error. Preserve that rule and use narrow typing.cast declarations at five standard-library stub gaps rather than adding runtime checks or disabling the rule.
- Tailwind 4.3.3 adds @parcel/watcher; Bun blocks its source-build lifecycle script, but the platform package path works and development/browser verification succeeds without trusting the script.
- Keep the existing picomatch 4.0.4 security override because OSV flags the older compatible line; the watcher path passes verification with the override.

Verification:
- Full just check passes: 1,189 JavaScript tests, 766 Python tests, all typechecks, lint, and goldens.
- Production just build passes.
- Browser development path verified by the user.
- Single-agent three-pass review completed; findings were fixed or skipped with documented context.
- GitLab dependency scanning remains required in the MR pipeline.

title: epic: Staff Review R2 — Architecture & Code Quality
description: 3 architecture issues from staff review R2. God component in detail-panel, duplicated node dimming logic, unsafe type assertions in build-resource-graph.

title: Use exception chaining instead of 'from None' in cli.py
description: cli.py:71-74 uses 'from None' to suppress tracebacks on FileNotFoundError and UnicodeDecodeError. Guideline says 'chain exceptions with from to preserve tracebacks'. The OSError handler on line 75-76 correctly uses 'from exc'. UnicodeDecodeError in particular carries byte position and encoding details useful for debugging. Consider using 'from exc' consistently.

title: Fix node ordering and edge weights in resource hierarchy layout
description: After renaming hierarchy root labels to 'Lakebase Autoscaling' and 'Lakebase Provisioned', the graph layout has weird connection weights/ordering. Nodes are not positioned well relative to each other. Needs investigation into ELK layout options — edge weights, node ordering constraints, or priority settings that may need adjusting for the renamed hierarchies.

title: Click on node fails during hover debounce period
close_reason: Won't fix — React Flow's click-while-moving behavior is acceptable. The 50ms hover debounce is fine as-is.

title: feat: add non-color diff indicators for color-blind users
description: Added (green) and modified (amber) nodes are indistinguishable for red-green color-blind users (~8% of males). Removed has dashed border which helps, but added/modified have no shape difference. Fix: add icon/shape differentiation — '+' for added, '~' for modified, '-' for removed — or use distinct border patterns (double/dotted/dashed).

title: Lateral sync edges for synced_database_table
description:
synced_database_table bridges the database and UC worlds — it references a database_instance_name AND a three-part UC table name (catalog.schema.table). Visualize this with a dashed lateral edge:

- Add left/right handles on synced_database_table and the referenced UC node
- Dashed stroke style (strokeDasharray) + distinct color to differentiate from hierarchy edges
- Configure ELK port positions so lateral edges exit from the side, not top/bottom
- ELK needs to know about cross-subgraph edges to place database and UC hierarchies side-by-side

This is a new visual concept — sync/mirror relationship vs parent-child.
close_reason: Sync edges implemented with ELK priority-based layout and correct UC→Lakebase edge direction

title: refactor: convert buildResourceGraph to functional style
description: build-resource-graph.ts lines 120+ uses imperative push/mutation internally (const nodes = []; nodes.push(...)) with a mutable Set and a mutating addEdge helper. This contrasts with the functional style used everywhere else in the codebase (buildPlanGraph uses map/flatMap/spread throughout). The same file's own buildResourceNode and buildGroupNode are pure — but the orchestrating function isn't. Refactor to use map/flatMap/spread for consistency with the project's functional philosophy.

title: Restyle lateral edges
description: Lateral edges render but look bad with smoothstep right-angle routing. Design idea: use top/bottom handles for lateral edges (instead of left/right hierarchy handles) and render them as straight lines that cut linearly across the graph, rendered on top of all nodes. This separates the two edge types visually — hierarchy flows left-to-right through side handles, lateral references cut vertically through top/bottom handles.

title: Add linter to repository
description: Add a linter (e.g. ESLint or Biome) to the repository for consistent code quality enforcement. Should integrate with the existing TypeScript strict setup and align with the functional coding philosophy in CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: Biome linter/formatter added and committed in e810c6d

title: FlowCanvasLayout not wrapped in React.memo
description:
flow-canvas-layout.tsx:60-155 — FlowCanvasLayout is a plain function component, not wrapped in React.memo. Its parent FlowCanvas re-renders on every hover state change.

Won't fix: React.memo wouldn't skip re-renders — nodes and edges props get new array refs on every hover (styledEdges recalculates based on hoveredNodeId, then spread copies shed readonly). The Panel children already short-circuit internally via stable props. False positive from review.

title: Color edges to match diff state of connected nodes
description: New edges (connecting added nodes) should be green, removed edges should be red with reduced opacity, matching the node diff-state styling. Currently all edges render in the default grey regardless of whether the connected resources are new, removed, or modified.

title: Add symlink/traversal/overwrite protection to output path
description: browser.py:55-58 passes user-supplied --output path directly to Path.write_text() with no validation. No symlink check, no traversal check, no O_EXCL for preventing overwrite of existing files. Risk is accidental overwrite rather than attack (local CLI tool), but defense-in-depth improvement. Consider resolving the path and checking for symlinks, or using O_EXCL mode for new files.
close_reason: Implemented _validate_output_path: symlink check + path.resolve() for traversal normalization

title: Audit codebase for more shared-pattern abstraction opportunities
description:
We just introduced LateralEdgeSpec to replace the bespoke extractDatabaseInstanceEdges pattern with a declarative spec + runner. This same approach — identifying a repeated loop-filter-extract-resolve-guard pattern and replacing it with a typed spec + generic runner — may apply elsewhere in the codebase.

Known candidates still using bespoke patterns:
- **Warehouse edges** (reverse index pattern) — dagshund-22l6
- **Serving endpoint model edges** (array traversal, one-to-many) — dagshund-2d4t
- **Pipeline target edges** (multiple paths + dedup)

Worth investigating:
- Are there other repeated patterns in graph building (e.g. TierSpec chain traversal, phantom node creation) that could benefit from further abstraction?
- Are there patterns in the Python text renderer that share structure?
- The chain spec system (UC_CHAIN, POSTGRES_CHAIN) already abstracts phantom node creation — are there other hierarchy-like patterns that could use ChainSpec?

Goal: identify 2-3 concrete candidates and evaluate whether abstraction would reduce code or just add indirection.

title: Unit tests for database-instance:: in resource-key
description: extractPhantomBadge and isPhantomLeaf were extended with database-instance:: prefix support but have no dedicated unit tests for it. The integration test covers the full path, but resource-key.test.ts should have explicit cases.

title: Connect trigger_quality task to data_quality_pipeline job
description: The trigger_quality task node should have an edge connecting it to the data_quality_pipeline job, but it currently renders disconnected. Investigate whether the edge is missing from the plan JSON parsing or from the graph building step.

title: feat: show diff state count badges on filter buttons
description: Filter buttons show 'Added', 'Modified', 'Removed' but no counts. Users can't tell at a glance how many nodes match. Fix: pass node counts to DiffFilterToolbar, display as 'Added (3)'. If count is 0, gray out the button.

title: Suppress or improve detail panel for root nodes
description: Root nodes (UC, Workspace, Postgres, Lakebase roots) open an empty detail panel when clicked — no meaningful content to show. Consider suppressing the detail panel for root nodes or showing a brief contextual message like phantom nodes have ('Untracked by this bundle').

title: render generated UC table for Postgres sync
description: Postgres synced table plan entries expose source_table_full_name (an original UC source reference) and synced_table_id (a real UC table managed as an output of the postgres_synced_tables resource). Implement separate semantics: keep source_table_full_name on the existing phantom/reference path; materialize valid three-part synced_table_id values as derived nodes with derivedKind ucSyncedTable, ownerResourceKey, registry-driven ID/badge/extraction/validation/rendering/promotion, owner-inherited diff state, no copied plan state, solid resource rendering, an unchanged derived-to-owner dependency edge, and owner navigation in the detail panel. Derived nodes must survive phantom filtering and preserve phantom ancestors. description:
Review the blanket rule in .agents/guidelines/WORKFLOW.md that prohibits Markdown files for plans, TODOs, and task lists.

This was discovered while preparing a detailed implementation handoff for dagshund-2a3q. The bead description can hold the implementation contract, but a deliberately written plan document may be easier for a weaker implementation model to consume, review, and execute than a long issue description.

Decide whether the workflow should continue prohibiting all Markdown implementation plans or permit a narrowly defined plan artifact while br remains the authoritative task tracker.

The review must address:
- The intended distinction between task tracking in br and a temporary implementation/handoff specification.
- Whether plan files improve model handoff enough to justify another artifact.
- How to prevent a Markdown plan and its bead from becoming conflicting sources of truth.
- Permitted location and naming if plans are allowed.

- Session-close expectations and whether plan files may be committed.
- Guidance for choosing a bead-only description versus a separate plan.

Do not relax the workflow opportunistically as part of another feature. Make an explicit policy decision, update WORKFLOW.md and any cross-references if approved, and keep the current prohibition if no clear lifecycle prevents drift.

Acceptance:
WORKFLOW.md states an unambiguous, internally consistent policy for detailed implementation handoffs. If Markdown plans are allowed, br remains the source of truth and the document lifecycle prevents stale duplicate tracking. If they remain prohibited, the workflow explains where detailed weaker-model implementation contracts belong and how they should be structured.

title: Visualize added/removed edges on modified tasks
description:
Currently edge diff state is inferred from endpoint nodes only (resolveEdgeDiffState in diff-state-styles.ts). If either endpoint is added/removed, the edge gets that state. But when a MODIFIED task changes its depends_on array (adds or removes a dependency), the edge has no diff state because both endpoint nodes still exist.

Example: task A depends_on [B, C]. After modification, task A depends_on [B, D]. The edge A→C should show as red/removed (ghost edge), and A→D should show as green/added. Currently A→C just disappears and A→D appears as gray/unchanged.

Implementation requires:
1. Compare old depends_on (from change old_value) vs new depends_on (from new_value) for modified tasks
2. Create ghost edges for removed dependencies — these edges exist in old state but not new state. Render red with reduced opacity.
3. Mark newly added edges (exist in new state but not old state) as added. Render green.
4. GraphEdge type needs a diffState field: 'added' | 'removed' | 'unchanged'
5. toFlowEdges() in layout-graph.ts needs to use the edge's own diffState when present, falling back to the current endpoint-inference logic

Key files:
- src/types/graph-types.ts (add diffState to GraphEdge)
- src/graph/extract-tasks.ts (extract old/new depends_on from changes)
- src/graph/build-plan-graph.ts (compare old vs new depends_on, create ghost edges, mark new edges)
- src/graph/layout-graph.ts (toFlowEdges should respect edge-level diffState)
- src/components/diff-state-styles.ts (resolveEdgeDiffState already handles the styling, just needs to check edge's own diffState first)
close_reason: Merged into dagshund-o4z — implementing ghost nodes and ghost edges together

title: Replace Any type aliases with proper typed structures
description:
## Problem

The foundational type aliases in `src/dagshund/__init__.py` use `Any`, violating the project's "unknown over any" guideline:

```python
from typing import Any

type ResourceChange = dict[str, Any]
type ResourceChangeMap = dict[str, ResourceChange]
type Plan = dict[str, Any]
```

This means every downstream access (`data.get("plan", {})`, `entry.get("action", "")`, etc.) is completely untyped. The TypeScript side has Zod schema validation at boundaries; the Python side has nothing equivalent.

## What to Do

Replace `Any`-based type aliases with properly typed structures. Options:

### Option A: TypedDict (recommended)
```python
from typing import TypedDict, NotRequired

class FieldChange(TypedDict):
    action: NotRequired[str]
    old: NotRequired[object]
    new: NotRequired[object]

class ResourceChange(TypedDict):
    action: NotRequired[str]
    changes: NotRequired[dict[str, FieldChange]]

type ResourceChangeMap = dict[str, ResourceChange]

class Plan(TypedDict):
    plan: NotRequired[ResourceChangeMap]
    cli_version: NotRequired[str]
    # ... other known top-level keys
```

Note: TypedDict uses `class` syntax but is NOT OOP — it's purely a type-level construct with no runtime behavior, no methods, no inheritance hierarchy. It's the Python equivalent of a TypeScript `interface` or a Zod schema. This is consistent with the project philosophy (same as how the TS side uses `interface` and `type` without it being OOP).

### Option B: Use `object` instead of `Any`
Minimal change: replace `Any` with `object` everywhere, forcing runtime type narrowing (`isinstance` checks) before use. Less ergonomic but maximally strict.

## Files That Will Need Updates
- `src/dagshund/__init__.py` — type definitions + `parse_plan` return type
- `src/dagshund/text.py` — all functions consuming ResourceChange/Plan
- `src/dagshund/browser.py` — `_inject_plan` parameter type
- `src/dagshund/cli.py` — if Plan type changes

## Acceptance Criteria
- No `Any` import or usage in `src/dagshund/`
- All type annotations use the new typed structures
- `just check` passes (including `ty` type checker)
- Existing tests pass without modification
close_reason: Won't fix: the plan data is genuinely Any from our perspective — we don't control the Databricks CLI schema. Value fields (old/new/remote) are polymorphic (strings, ints, dicts, lists). TypedDict would still need Any for those, giving minimal benefit for the complexity. Runtime isinstance guards from the input hardening issue handle malformed data.

title: Design CI/CD pipeline structure
description:
Final pipeline design for watertight CI. Output of this bead is the design below; implementation lands via dagshund-39ue (golden + CI refactor) and dagshund-21qe (browser smoke). This bead stays open until the human approves closing.

## Pipeline structure

| Trigger | Jobs | Target duration |
|---|---|---|
| Feature branch push (non-docs/beads) | quality + golden | ~45s |
| PR opened / PR push | quality + golden + security + browser | ~3 min |
| Merge to main (non-docs/beads) | pages | ~45s |
| Tag v* | version-check + build + smoke-wheel + publish-test + publish (unchanged) | ~2 min + manual gates |

## Workflow rules (mandatory)

- **Docs/beads skip:** pipeline does not run when every changed file matches \`**.md\` or \`.beads/**\`. Any non-matching file triggers normal flow. Applies to feature branches, MRs, AND main pushes (so chore(beads): sync does not rebuild pages).
- **MR-then-branch:** if an MR is open for the branch, the branch pipeline does not run — only the MR pipeline runs. Prevents doubled cost on PR pushes.
- **Interruptible:** all non-release jobs (interruptible: true). Release jobs (build, smoke-wheel, publish-test, publish) are NOT interruptible.

## Job definitions

### quality (feature branch + MR)
Lint + typecheck + unit tests as one job:
- biome check + ruff check
- tsc --noEmit + ty check (typecheck is mandatory — prek can be bypassed)
- bun test + pytest

### golden (feature branch + MR) — renamed from smoke-text
- text/md diffing (exists today)
- NEW: exit code assertions (dagshund -e vs expected-exit.txt)
- NEW: graph structure assertions (Bun extractor vs expected-graph.json)
- NEW: filter variant diffing (fixtures/golden/filters/ only)

### security (MR only — moved from every push)
sast + secret_detection. Runs scan against full repo state, not diff — redundant on feature branches when MR pipeline runs on the same commit.

### browser (MR only) — new
build-template + Playwright headless Chromium over 3 fixtures (mixed-changes, all-hierarchies, no-changes). Asserts no console errors + node count > 0 + diff badges present. Dedicated Playwright image, version-pinned (never :latest).

### pages (main only, now subject to docs/beads skip)

### Release chain (tag only, unchanged)
version-check → build → smoke-wheel → publish-test → publish.

## Golden fixture contract

Each fixtures/golden/<name>/ contains:
- before/databricks.yaml
- after/databricks.yaml
- plan.json
- expected.txt
- expected.md
- expected-exit.txt (single line: 0, 2, or 3)
- expected-graph.json (node/edge/lateral/phantom counts + manifest)

### Filter variants — one dedicated fixture only
fixtures/golden/filters/ additionally contains:
- expected.changes-only.txt
- expected.added.txt
- expected.removed.txt
- expected.modified.txt
- expected.filter-type-jobs.txt
- expected.filter-field.txt

Dot-separated naming. Other fixtures do NOT have filter variants.

### expected-graph.json shape
{
  \"nodes\": { \"total\": N, \"by_kind\": { \"job\": N, \"task\": N, \"alert\": N, \"phantom\": N } },
  \"edges\": { \"total\": N, \"dag\": N, \"lateral\": N },
  \"laterals\": [ { \"source\": \"...\", \"target\": \"...\", \"kind\": \"...\" } ],
  \"phantoms\": [ { \"id\": \"...\", \"kind\": \"...\" } ]
}

Extractor is a Bun script that imports the same graph-builder modules the browser uses, prints JSON to stdout.

## Caching (mandatory, budget-critical)

.release-setup before_script currently re-downloads bun and runs fresh uv sync + bun install every job. Add cache: directives keyed on uv.lock + js/bun.lock, caching .uv-cache/ + js/node_modules/. Set UV_CACHE_DIR=.uv-cache in variables. Saves ~30-60s per job extending .release-setup.

## Enterprise fixtures

All golden fixtures run identically in CI regardless of tier — CI only needs committed plan.json, not Databricks auth. Enterprise tier affects regeneration only. Convention: enterprise fixtures under fixtures/golden/enterprise/<name>/. Not blocking this design.

## Budget estimate (500 min/month GitLab free tier)

At 60 feature pushes + 10 MR pushes + 8 main-merges + 2 tag releases per month:
- 60 × 45s ≈ 45 min
- 10 × 3 min ≈ 30 min
- 8 × 45s ≈ 6 min
- 2 × 2 min ≈ 4 min
Total: ~85 min/month. With interruptible collapsing bursts: realistically 60-70 min/month.

## What this bead does NOT specify
- Exact Playwright image tag → 21qe picks a specific pinned version
- Exact cache:key granularity → 39ue tunes during implementation
- Enterprise fixture introduction → future bead

title: Split create/delete diffs into per-field entries
description:
Redesign detail panel to show three clearly labeled sections for any node: Added (create), Modified (update), Unchanged.

## Added (create) — for new tasks or new fields on modified tasks
Instead of one giant JSON blob, break into individual field entries. Each field (depends_on, notebook_task, task_key) gets its own card with green + styling. For a fully new task, the header says "this task was created" and each field is shown as its own create entry.

## Modified (update) — for changed fields
Current behavior is good: shows old value with - red, new value with + green (structural diff). Additionally:
- If a key is REMOVED from a modified task (e.g. depends_on deleted entirely), show it in red with - as its own entry in this section
- If a key is ADDED to a modified task, show it in green with + as its own entry

## Unchanged — for fields that didn't change
Renamed from "Unmodified Configuration". Shows resource state fields not involved in any change, neutral styling.

## Removed (delete) — for deleted tasks or removed fields
Mirror of create: each field gets its own card in red with - styling. "This task was deleted, here's what it had."

## Section ordering
Added → Modified → Unchanged (or just the relevant ones depending on node diffState)

- src/components/detail-panel.tsx (main rendering logic, ChangeEntry, ResourceStateView)
- src/utils/structural-diff.ts (computeStructuralDiff)
