title: Replace group nodes with generic chain spec and phantom traversal
description:
Refactor the resource graph node model and hierarchy building logic.

## Current problems
1. 'resource-group' nodeKind conflates three roles: root anchors, hierarchy containers, and phantom nodes
2. Container resources (postgres_projects, database_instances) render as both a group node AND a resource node (duplication bug)
3. Phantom creation is scattered across 5+ code paths, each special-cased per hierarchy
4. Phantom chains don't fully walk up (phantom branch skips to root instead of creating phantom project)
5. HierarchySpec only supports one mid-tier, can't extend to deeper chains

## New design

### Node kinds
Replace 'resource-group' with clean taxonomy:
- resource: anything from the plan (including containers)
- root: hierarchy anchors (UC, Workspace) — structural only
- phantom: inferred nodes to complete hierarchy chains

### Chain spec
Generic tier-based hierarchy definition:
- Each hierarchy is an ordered list of TierSpecs (root-adjacent → leaf)
- Each tier defines: resourceTypes, resolveIdentity, resolveParentRef, deriveParentRef, phantomId
- One generic traversal function walks up from any resource, creating phantoms for missing ancestors
- Replaces all scattered phantom logic with a single mechanism

### What changes
- New types: TierSpec, ChainSpec (in graph-types.ts)
- New function: generic chain traversal (replaces buildHierarchySubgraph, buildPhantomSchemaNodes, sync phantom logic)
- Remove 'resource-group' nodeKind entirely
- Update React components: ResourceGroupNode → split into RootNode + PhantomNode (or unified with ResourceNode)
- Update detail panel to handle new node kinds
- Update all tests

## Out of scope
- Reworking specific hierarchy definitions (Postgres/Lakebase relationships) — separate beads
- Cross-hierarchy reference edges (dagshund-czfs)
- The dev CSS fix (separate commit)
close_reason: Replaced resource-group with root/phantom nodeKinds. Generic chain spec traversal for phantom creation. Container dedup eliminates duplicate group+resource nodes.

title: graph: resolve Lakebase endpoint parent resource refs
description:
During dagshund-3l7p Lakebase fixture work, the browser resource graph showed a created Lakebase endpoint detached from its created branch. The plan entry for the created endpoint has a semantic parent field that is still a bundle resource-id expression, not a concrete Lakebase path:

    resources.postgres_endpoints.dev_endpoint:
      action: create
      depends_on:
        - node: resources.postgres_branches.dev_branch
      new_state:
        value:
          endpoint_id: primary
          parent: "${resources.postgres_branches.dev_branch.id}"
          endpoint_type: ENDPOINT_TYPE_READ_WRITE
        vars:
          parent: "${resources.postgres_branches.dev_branch.id}"

By contrast, skipped/remote endpoints expose a concrete parent path such as:

    parent: projects/dagshund/branches/prd

Current graph code in js/src/graph/build-resource-graph.ts parses concrete Postgres endpoint parent paths, but does not resolve bundle resource-id references in the parent field. As a result, endpoint -> branch hierarchy is lost for create-time endpoints whose parent is "${resources.postgres_branches.<name>.id}".

Important constraint: do NOT use depends_on to build this hierarchy. depends_on remains deployment ordering and is intentionally ignored for resource graph construction. The fix should use the semantic parent field only.

Expected fix shape:
- Recognize bundle resource-id refs in Postgres hierarchy parent fields, e.g. "${resources.postgres_branches.dev_branch.id}".
- Resolve endpoint parent refs directly to the referenced branch resource node when that branch exists in the plan.
- Preserve existing concrete path handling for parents like projects/<project>/branches/<branch>.
- Preserve fallback/phantom behavior when no concrete path or resolvable parent resource ref exists.
- Consider the same parent-ref helper for postgres_branches.parent if projects ever appear as "${resources.postgres_projects.<name>.id}", but do not broaden beyond semantic parent fields.

Add a focused JS test in js/tests/graph/build-resource-graph.test.ts where a postgres_endpoints create entry has parent "${resources.postgres_branches.dev_branch.id}" and assert the graph contains:

    resources.postgres_branches.dev_branch -> resources.postgres_endpoints.dev_endpoint

and does not attach the endpoint directly under postgres-root.

Repro fixture context: fixtures/golden/lakebase-autoscaling/plan.json from dagshund-3l7p.
close_reason: done: delivered in completed Lakebase fixture and graph work

title: make Parcel watcher load in Nix dev shell
description:
`nix develop --command just build` fails during Tailwind CSS startup because Parcel's native watcher cannot load the C++ runtime:

```
error: libstdc++.so.6: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
code: ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED
at js/node_modules/@parcel/watcher/index.js:16
```

Evidence:
- The dev shell has an empty `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
- `ldd js/node_modules/@parcel/watcher-linux-x64-glibc/watcher.node` reports `libstdc++.so.6 => not found`.
- Nix store GCC runtime outputs containing `lib/libstdc++.so.6` exist, but the native module has no runtime path to them.
- Lint, type checks, JS tests, Python tests, and golden checks all pass; failure occurs before project assets compile.

Expected behavior:
- A fresh declared dev shell can run `just build` without imperative host packages or ad hoc environment overrides.
- Fix the Nix declaration so the native Parcel watcher can locate its required runtime libraries.
- Verify `nix develop --command just build` and `nix develop --command just check` from a clean checkout.

Discovered while verifying `dagshund-7gck`.

title: unify drift vocabulary across field/topology/list-element renderings
description:
## Observed

In `fixtures/golden/manual-drift/expected.txt` (and `.md`), three entries are all semantically "manual edit that apply will overwrite" but render with three different vocabularies:

    ~ edit_mode: "EDITABLE" -> "UI_LOCKED" (drift)
    - tasks[task_key='publish'].depends_on[task_key='ingest']: {task_key: "ingest"} (drift)
    + tasks[task_key='publish'].depends_on[task_key='transform'] (re-added)
    + tasks[task_key='transform'] (re-added)

| Case | Shape | Current tag |
|---|---|---|
| Scalar field drift | `old==new, remote differs` | `(drift)` |
| Topology re-add (sub-entity missing from server) | `old==new, no remote` | `(re-added)` |
| List-element delete (in remote, not in new) — added by dagshund-1naj | `remote-only` on a bundle-managed list key | `(drift)` |

The split between `(drift)` and `(re-added)` pre-dates dagshund-1naj — `(re-added)` has always been the topology-drift renderer's phrasing. dagshund-1naj just introduced a third case that joined the `(drift)` bucket, which makes the inconsistency more visible.

## Proposal

Unify under verb-explicit tags so the reader doesn't have to decode which bucket they're in:

    ~ edit_mode: "EDITABLE" -> "UI_LOCKED" (will overwrite)
    - tasks[...].depends_on[task_key='ingest']: {...} (will remove)
    + tasks[...].depends_on[task_key='transform'] (will re-add)
    + tasks[task_key='transform'] (will re-add)

Benefits:
- Tells the reader what apply will do, not just "there is a drift"
- Symmetric across directions (+/~/-) — the tag and the symbol agree
- Removes the `(re-added)` / `(drift)` split entirely

Costs:
- Golden churn across manual-drift + any other drift-bearing fixtures
- Vocabulary change surfaces in docs (`README.md`, `SKILL.md`) and in the CHANGELOG for consumers grepping output

## Scope

- `src/dagshund/format.py` — `format_field_suffix` drift-tag branches, `_iter_drift_warning_lines` re-added phrasing
- `src/dagshund/terminal.py` / `src/dagshund/markdown.py` — the topology-drift `(re-added)` rendering
- Browser: `js/src/components/detail-panel/` — DriftPill + any "drift" copy in ChangeEntry / SectionDivider
- Golden fixtures: regenerate anything with drift (`manual-drift`, plus any others after grep)
- README screenshots may need re-shooting if the terminal output is pictured

## Alternatives

1. Unify everything under `(drift)` and drop `(re-added)` — loses "what will happen" specificity
2. Keep `(re-added)`, change `(drift)` deletes to `(will remove)` — partial consistency only
3. Do nothing — tolerate the existing asymmetry

Recommend option in "Proposal" section. The verb-explicit form reads as well for screen readers and for users scanning a large plan.

## Out of scope

- The `(remote)` tag for fields the bundle doesn't manage — that's a different semantic ("server owns this, apply does nothing"), not drift. Keep as-is or switch to `(unmanaged)` / `(server owns)` as a separate question.

## Context

Discovered while reviewing dagshund-1naj output. Not a bug — a polish/clarity improvement. Priority 3 (backlog).

title: Decompose oversized functions and replace mutation with functional patterns
description:
## Problem

Four functions exceed the 20-line guideline, and three functions use imperative mutation (list.append, dict.setdefault) instead of functional patterns (generators, comprehensions). These overlap — the oversized functions are often the ones with mutation.

## Oversized Functions

### 1. `_render_resource` — ~34 logic lines
- **File**: `src/dagshund/text.py`, around lines 93-132
- Handles both the resource header AND field-level change details
- **Fix**: Extract field-change rendering into a separate function (e.g., `_render_field_changes`)
- Also uses `list.append()` mutation — replace with `yield` (make it a generator) or build via comprehension

### 2. `build_parser` — ~29 lines
- **File**: `src/dagshund/cli.py`, around lines 18-47
- Largely declarative argparse configuration, so complexity is low
- **Fix**: Could extract argument groups into helper functions, but this is low priority given it's purely declarative

### 3. `main` — ~26 lines
- **File**: `src/dagshund/cli.py`, around lines 72-97
- Handles argument parsing, branching (browser vs text), error handling, exit
- **Fix**: Extract browser branch (lines ~82-90) and text branch (lines ~91-94) into separate functions

### 4. `render_text` — borderline at ~21 lines
- **File**: `src/dagshund/text.py`, around lines 197-219
- Right at the limit, may not need changes after other refactoring

## Mutation Patterns to Replace

### 1. `_render_resource` — `lines.append()`
- Builds a `list[str]` via repeated `.append()` calls across ~30 lines
- **Fix**: Convert to a generator that `yield`s lines, or build via comprehension/concatenation

### 2. `_group_by_resource_type` — `dict.setdefault().append()`
- **File**: `src/dagshund/text.py`, around lines 156-162
- Builds a dict of lists imperatively
- **Fix**: Use `itertools.groupby` on sorted input, or a comprehension-based approach

### 3. `_print_summary` — `summary_parts.append()`
- **File**: `src/dagshund/text.py`, around lines 182-189
- Builds a list then joins it
- **Fix**: Replace with a generator expression inside `", ".join(...)`

## Acceptance Criteria
- No function in `src/dagshund/` exceeds 20 lines of logic
- No `list.append()` or `dict.setdefault()` mutation patterns — use generators, comprehensions, or `itertools`
- All existing tests pass without modification
- `just check` passes
close_reason: All mutation patterns replaced, all functions under 20 lines, pattern matching for type dispatch

title: Render DAG with diff-state colored nodes in React Flow
description:
Wire the graph model into React Flow rendering with visual diff-state distinction. Minimal styling — just enough to tell states apart.

DEPENDS ON: dagshund-ebk (graph model must exist first)

DATA CONTEXT:
The graph model produces three kinds of nodes:
- Job nodes (nodeKind='job'): represent the resource itself, contain metadata (name, triggers, compute)
- Task nodes (nodeKind='task'): individual tasks within a job, form the DAG via depends_on edges
- The user wants to see BOTH: the job as context/container and the tasks as the interactive DAG

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. Custom React Flow node components:
   - src/components/task-node.tsx — renders a task node with diff-state color coding:
     - added: green border/accent
     - removed: red border, reduced opacity (40%)
     - modified: amber/yellow accent
     - unchanged: neutral/default (zinc/gray)
   - src/components/job-node.tsx — renders job metadata (name, etc.) as a header/container node
   Keep it simple — colored border or background tint is enough for now. No fancy visuals yet.

2. Update App.tsx to:
   - Accept a Plan object as prop or via context
   - Call graph model functions to get React Flow nodes/edges
   - Pass custom node types to ReactFlow
   - For now, use a hardcoded test plan or accept via window.__DAGSHUND_PLAN__ global (stdin feature will wire this up)

3. Custom hook (src/hooks/use-plan-graph.ts):
   - Takes Plan, returns { nodes, edges } ready for React Flow
   - Memoized with useMemo

CONSTRAINTS:
- Function components only, no classes
- All readonly where possible
- Register custom node types properly with React Flow nodeTypes (must be stable reference, not inline object)
- Must handle empty plan gracefully (no nodes = empty canvas, not a crash)
- Dark background (zinc-950 already set in App.tsx) — colors should work on dark
- Handle multiple jobs producing separate sub-graphs within the same canvas
close_reason: Custom job/task nodes with diff-state coloring, usePlanGraph hook, App wired with mixed-plan fixture. 51 tests passing, tsc clean.

title: Support detailed exit codes for CI usage (like terraform plan)
description:
Support detailed exit codes for CI usage, similar to terraform plan -detailed-exitcode.

## Exit codes (opt-in via flag)
- Exit 0: plan parsed, no changes (all resources have action 'skip')
- Exit 1: error (bad input, missing file, etc.)
- Exit 2: plan parsed, changes detected (at least one resource has a non-skip action)

## Key discovery
Databricks includes ALL managed resources in plan output, even unchanged ones. Unchanged resources have `"action": "skip"` at the top level. So `plan["plan"]` being non-empty does NOT mean drift.

Drift detection logic:
```python
has_changes = any(
    entry.get("action") not in ("skip", "")
    for entry in plan.values()
)
```

## Fixture
`fixtures/no-changes-plan.json` — real plan output where nothing changed. All 8 resources have `"action": "skip"`.

## Open questions
- Flag name: --detailed-exitcode (terraform convention) vs shorter alternative
- Applies to both text and browser modes
- Interaction with dagshund-cfx: empty plan (no plan key / empty dict) is still exit 1 (error). A plan full of skips is exit 0 (success, no changes). These are different situations.

title: Share Python reporting decisions across renderers
description:
Context
The Python architecture review found that terminal.py and markdown.py independently coordinate nearly the same report workflow: filtering, grouping, resource effects, drift details, wheel suppression, field changes, reentries, summaries, and warnings. Output-specific strings legitimately differ, but repeated selection and categorization require synchronized edits whenever semantics evolve.

Objective
Share the non-format-specific reporting decisions while retaining straightforward, separate terminal and Markdown rendering functions.

Scope
- src/dagshund/terminal.py, src/dagshund/markdown.py, and relevant reporting helpers currently in format.py.
- Consume the domain decisions established by the centralize-plan-semantics bead rather than creating another interpretation layer.
- Focus on repeated field selection, categorization, and report aggregation. Do not extract trivial expressions merely because they look similar.

Acceptance criteria
- Shared selection and categorization cover ordinary field changes, topology reentries, wheel-suppressed changes and summaries, and deploy-triggered run details where both formats have the same contract.
- Existing common filtering and grouping helpers remain shared; terminal and Markdown do not independently reimplement the same semantic policy.
- Preserve each output contract: ordering, counts, filtered visibility, unchanged-parent effects, warning scope, terminal colors/wrapping, Markdown links, and wheel suppression.
- Existing golden terminal and Markdown outputs remain byte-identical to the baseline after any explicitly approved semantic corrections from the prerequisite task.
- Add or strengthen behavioral tests proving both renderers select equivalent information on mixed drift, effect, filter, and wheel-update cases while retaining their format-specific output.
- Follow repository workflow, including just check and just build in the Nix shell for implementation verification.

Constraints and exclusions
No renderer superclass, plugin system, generic document AST, new dependencies, or speculative abstraction. Keep actual string formatting output-specific. No debug tracing changes, parser/schema policy changes, frontend changes, or state-access cleanup. Normalization ownership has its own bead; avoid introducing a competing orchestration convention here.
close_reason: Shared Python reporting selection and aggregation across terminal and Markdown while preserving format-specific output. Mixed behavioral tests, just check, byte-identical goldens, just build, browser verification, and three-pass review passed.

title: detail panel: add hover tooltips to ActionBadge and DiffStateBadge
description:
## Observed

In the detail panel, DriftPill is the only badge/pill component that carries a `title` tooltip (`Differs from remote — apply will reconcile this`). Every other small indicator renders bare text:

- `ActionBadge` (`action-badge.tsx`) — shows `create` / `update` / `update_id` / `delete` / `recreate` / `resize` / `remote`. No tooltip explaining what the action means.
- `DiffStateBadge` (`diff-state-badge.tsx`) — shows `added` / `modified` / `removed` / `unchanged` / `unknown`. No tooltip.
- `DriftPill` (`drift-pill.tsx`) — has a tooltip today, but the copy is generic across three semantically distinct drift cases (topology re-add, field drift, reclassified list-element delete → Removed on apply).

New readers have to read the code or the docs to tell `update_id` from `recreate` from `resize`, or understand why `added` + drift means "re-added on apply" vs a fresh create. Hover tooltips are a cheap, low-surface way to explain these inline.

## Proposal

### 1. ActionBadge

Add a `title` keyed by action:

    create      → 'Will be created'
    update      → 'Will be updated in place'
    update_id   → 'Will be re-keyed (identifier change)'
    delete      → 'Will be deleted'
    recreate    → 'Will be deleted and recreated'
    resize      → 'Will be resized (cluster/compute)'
    remote      → 'Present on the remote, not managed by this bundle'

Fall through to the action string for unknown actions.

### 2. DiffStateBadge

Add a `title` keyed by diffState:

    added       → 'This resource will be created on apply'
    modified    → 'This resource has field-level changes'
    removed     → 'This resource will be removed on apply'
    unchanged   → 'No changes planned'
    unknown     → 'State could not be determined'

### 3. DriftPill

Thread a `variant` prop (or equivalent) so the caller can pick copy per drift case:

    <DriftPill variant=\"re-add\" />    → 'Missing from remote — apply will re-add this'
    <DriftPill variant=\"overwrite\" /> → 'Remote differs from bundle — apply will overwrite this'
    <DriftPill variant=\"remove\" />    → 'Added manually on the remote — apply will remove this'

Pill text (\`drift\`) stays identical across variants per the qby2 decision — only the tooltip varies.

## Call sites to wire variant into DriftPill

- \`change-entry.tsx\` — has \`isDrift\` + \`diffResult\`, can derive variant from \`diff.kind\` / \`semantic\`
- \`drift-reentry-section.tsx\` — always \`re-add\`
- \`drift-removal-section.tsx\` (added in dagshund-3hdx) — always \`remove\`
- \`task-changes-summary.tsx\` — per-task, has \`isDrift\`; would need drift kind propagated through \`TaskChangeSummary\`
- \`task-node.tsx\` / \`resource-node.tsx\` — node-level drift; would need drift kind on \`DagNodeData\`
- \`detail-panel.tsx\` — \`isDriftNode\` header case

Some callers (graph nodes, task summary) don't currently carry drift-kind info — may need schema/derivation changes.

## Out of scope

- Changing the visible pill text (qby2 established \`drift\` as category label)
- Section-level prose changes (owned by dagshund-3hdx, now shipped)
- Rich popover/overlay tooltips — native \`title\` is enough; no new dependency

## Discovered from

dagshund-qby2 — while unifying per-entry drift vocabulary, the generic pill tooltip was chosen as a minimal fix. The follow-up broadened in scope to cover all detail-panel badges after noticing DriftPill is the only one with hover help today.

title: Lateral edges + phantoms for app genie_space, database, and nested app references
description:
The AppResource schema allows three additional reference types not yet handled:

1. genie_space — has space_id. genie_spaces is not currently a bundle resource type but could appear as a reference target.
2. database — has instance_name, database_name, permission. Marked x-databricks-preview: PRIVATE. Postgres-related.

All low priority. Cannot be tested via golden fixtures — these resource types are unstable/preview and cannot be deployed on free edition. Implement when these resource types stabilize or show up in real plans. Test via unit tests with mock plan data.

title: agent skills: add neutral contracts and workflow wrappers
description:
Review the repo's agent-facing workflow files against model-agnostic skill best practices. Current shape is good: .codex skills and .claude commands stay thin, while AGENTS.md plus docs/workflows/*.md are the neutral source of truth. Improve the contract surface without duplicating workflow steps.

Scope:
- Add explicit Contract sections to .codex/skills/dagshund-release/SKILL.md and .codex/skills/dagshund-update-fixtures/SKILL.md. Suggested fields: Use when, Do not use when, Required inputs, Required approvals, External tools/services, Successful output, Failure behavior, Hard stops.
- Consider whether the Claude command docs need similarly short trigger/exclusion language, while keeping .claude thin and pointed at neutral docs.
- Evaluate small deterministic helpers for the highest-risk prose-driven workflow steps: release SHA resolution, MR/pipeline state checks, Databricks CLI release verification, fixture drift comparison, and manual-drift sanity checks. Prefer existing just/tooling patterns and avoid new dependencies.
- Decide whether repo-owned routing metadata or routing fixtures are useful now. Current routing is delegated to host tooling through skill/command names and descriptions; accidental triggering seems low because the workflows are narrow, so any added routing structure should solve a real problem rather than duplicate host behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Skills have clear trigger and exclusion contracts readable by Codex and other agents.
- Neutral workflow docs remain the source of truth; agent-specific entry points do not duplicate step-by-step process.
- Any proposed wrappers are tracked or implemented only where they reduce real command drift or safety risk.
- Routing metadata decision is documented, including why a repo-owned router file or routing eval fixture is or is not worthwhile right now.

title: Replace string-derived 'changed' property with explicit boolean field
description: _ActionConfig.changed in text.py:43-44 derives semantics from display string (self.display \!= 'unchanged'). This couples presentation to logic — if someone renames the display label, behavior silently changes. Add an explicit 'changed: bool = True' field to _ActionConfig and set changed=False on the 'skip' entry instead.

title: Terminal width-aware line wrapping for CLI output
description:
Use `os.get_terminal_size().columns` to detect terminal width and wrap long lines with proper continuation indentation instead of letting the terminal wrap at arbitrary points.

**Approach:** Build lines inline as we do now. If a line exceeds the terminal width, wrap it at semantic boundaries (commas between list/dict items, `->` separator) with continuation indented to the field's indent level + offset. Falls back to 80 columns when piped (no tty).

**Lower bound:** Set a minimum width (e.g. 60-80 chars) below which we don't attempt smart wrapping — if your terminal is that narrow, you just live with the wrapping. Above that threshold, lines are wrapped to fit.

**Applies to:** All CLI output lines — field changes (transitions, single values), resource headers. Not just transitions. The multiline block rendering for large single values stays as-is (it's already formatted for readability).

**Open questions:**
- Exact lower bound threshold
- Dumb wrap (textwrap on whitespace) vs structure-aware wrap (break at commas, `->`)
- Whether markdown output should also respect a configurable width or stay unwrapped (markdown renderers handle their own wrapping)

title: CLI --filter flag with search DSL from browser UI
description:
Port the browser search DSL to the CLI as a --filter / -f flag for text output.

The browser already has a search DSL (js/src/utils/search-query-parser.ts) with four token kinds:
- type:X — match resource type badge (jobs, volumes, schemas, etc.)
- status:X — match diff state (added, modified, removed, unchanged)
- "exact" — exact name match
- bare words — fuzzy text match against resource name

All tokens AND together. Same semantics on the CLI.

Examples:
  dagshund plan.json -f 'type:jobs'
  dagshund plan.json -f 'status:added'
  dagshund plan.json -f 'type:volumes status:removed'
  dagshund plan.json -f '"etl_pipeline"'

Composes with --changes-only (dagshund-37yu): filter first, then suppress unchanged within the filtered set.

Implementation notes:
- Python reimplements the tokenizer/matcher (no shared code with JS, but same grammar)
- Matching targets: resource type from the key prefix, action mapped to diff state, resource name
- Empty filter result = no output (not an error)
- No effect on browser mode (-o)

Design consideration: When implementing, consider refactoring _print_resource_groups to accept a predicate function (Callable[[ResourceChange], bool]) instead of the current frozenset[DiffState]. This would let the DSL filter and the diff state filter compose naturally as combined predicates, and avoids coupling the rendering layer to specific filter types.

title: Rename non-verb-first functions to match naming convention
description:
## Problem

Three private functions in `src/dagshund/text.py` use noun/adjective names instead of the required verb-first naming convention. The project guidelines require: "Descriptive names. Verb-first (extractJobTaskEdges not getEdges). No abbreviations."

## Functions to Rename

### 1. `_action_style` → `_resolve_action_style`
- **File**: `src/dagshund/text.py`, around line 54
- Returns `(color, symbol)` tuple for an action string
- "action_style" is a noun phrase; "resolve" makes it verb-first
- Used in: `_render_resource`, `_print_summary`

### 2. `_display_action` → `_map_display_action`
- **File**: `src/dagshund/text.py`, around line 59
- Maps internal action names to user-facing display names
- "display" is ambiguous (noun or verb); "map" clarifies intent
- Used in: `_render_resource`

### 3. `_all_unchanged` → `_check_all_unchanged`
- **File**: `src/dagshund/text.py`, around line 192
- Returns bool indicating whether every resource is unchanged
- "all_unchanged" is an adjective; "check" makes it verb-first
- Alternative: `_is_all_unchanged` (Python predicate convention)
- Used in: `render_text`

## Scope
- Rename the function definitions
- Update all call sites within `src/dagshund/text.py`
- Update all references in test files (`tests/test_text.py`) — the tests import these private functions directly
- Grep the entire repo to make sure no other references are missed

## Acceptance Criteria
- All three functions renamed with verb-first names
- All call sites and test references updated
- `just check` passes
- No stale references to old names anywhere in the repo

1. Move deepEqual to its own util, delete deepEqualRec

title: Fix Lakebase hierarchy: identity fields, resource path parsing, rename, fixture
description:
The Lakebase (formerly 'Lakebase Autoscaling') hierarchy has multiple issues from synthetic fixture data and incorrect field assumptions.

## What's wrong

1. **Identity fields**: Code uses `name` for project/branch identity. Real fields are `project_id` and `branch_id`.
2. **Parent references**: Code treats `parent` as a bare name. Real format is resource paths:
   - Branch `parent`: `projects/{project_id}` → points to project
   - Endpoint `parent`: `projects/{project_id}/branches/{branch_id}` → points to branch
3. **Root label**: 'Lakebase Autoscaling' should be just 'Lakebase'
4. **Fixture data**: `all-hierarchies-plan.json` uses wrong field names (`name` instead of `project_id`/`branch_id`/`endpoint_id`, bare names instead of resource paths for `parent`)

## What needs to change

### Code (build-resource-graph.ts)
- POSTGRES_CHAIN tier 0 (project): `resolveIdentity` should extract `project_id` not `name`
- POSTGRES_CHAIN tier 1 (branch): `resolveIdentity` should extract `branch_id` not `name`; `resolveParentRef` should parse `projects/{project_id}` to extract project_id
- POSTGRES_CHAIN tier 2 (endpoint): `resolveParentRef` should parse `projects/{project_id}/branches/{branch_id}` to extract branch_id
- Rename `rootLabel` from 'Lakebase Autoscaling' to 'Lakebase'

### Fixture (all-hierarchies-plan.json)
- Update postgres_projects to use `project_id`, `display_name`, `pg_version` (not `name`, `comment`)
- Update postgres_branches to use `branch_id`, `parent: projects/{project_id}`, `is_protected`, `no_expiry` (not `name`, `parent: bare_name`)
- Update postgres_endpoints to use `endpoint_id`, `parent: projects/{project_id}/branches/{branch_id}`, `endpoint_type` (not `name`, `parent: bare_name`, `type`)
- Add realistic field values matching the docs example

### Real field reference (from docs)

**Project fields**: project_id, display_name, pg_version, history_retention_duration, default_endpoint_settings
**Branch fields**: branch_id, parent (projects/{project_id}), source_branch (projects/{project_id}/branches/{branch_id}), is_protected, no_expiry, expire_time, ttl, source_branch_lsn, source_branch_time
**Endpoint fields**: endpoint_id, parent (projects/{project_id}/branches/{branch_id}), endpoint_type (ENDPOINT_TYPE_READ_WRITE|ENDPOINT_TYPE_READ_ONLY), autoscaling_limit_min_cu, autoscaling_limit_max_cu, disabled, no_suspension, suspend_timeout_duration, settings

### Tests
- Update test cases in build-resource-graph.test.ts to use correct field names and resource path formats

### Optional (separate bead)
- Model `source_branch` as a non-hierarchy provenance edge between branches
close_reason: Identity fields, resource path parsing, root rename, and fixture all updated to match real Databricks API

title: Add debug logging and verbose output
description:
Two distinct layers of additional output:

1. **Debug logging** (stdlib logging module, --debug / -d flag or DAGSHUND_DEBUG=1)
   - Traces the full pipeline: input source (file/stdin), JSON parse result, plan extraction, resource grouping, rendering path (text vs browser)
   - Uses Python logging at DEBUG level — conventional, composable with other tools
   - Outputs to stderr so it doesn't interfere with stdout rendering

2. **Verbose mode** (--verbose / -v flag)
   - Extra user-facing information: resource counts per type, field change counts, timing, plan metadata details
   - Not developer diagnostics — useful operational detail for the user

Both should be independent flags that can be combined. Debug implies verbose.

Scope: full pipeline coverage across cli.py, __init__.py, text.py, browser.py.
close_reason: Already implemented in a previous session

title: perf: fix O(n²) algorithms in layout-graph.ts
description: Two algorithmic inefficiencies: (1) topologicalSortTasks (lines 99-117) uses Array.shift() which is O(n) per call, making the overall BFS O(n²) instead of O(n+E). Fix: use index-based queue (maintain front pointer). (2) buildElkCompoundGraph (lines 170-180) filters edges with O(T*E) linear scans via .some(). Fix: build a Set of task IDs per group and use .has() for O(1) lookup. Both are theoretical concerns for typical Databricks DAG sizes but easy fixes.

title: fix: edge colors don't update on theme toggle
description: getEdgeStyle in diff-state-styles.ts calls getComputedStyle to resolve CSS variables at layout time, baking in the values. When the user toggles theme, edges retain old colors while nodes update. Fix: use var(--edge-added) etc as inline style values instead of resolved colors, so the browser resolves them reactively.

title: Review golden fixtures for clarity and coverage
description:
Walk through each golden fixture directory and evaluate: (1) Is the fixture name clear and descriptive? (2) Does it test a distinct, meaningful scenario? (3) Are there redundant or missing cases? (4) Do the fixture contents (YAML, expected output) match what the name promises? Human-driven review — go fixture by fixture together.

Fixtures need to be extended to cover:
- Dashboard resources with warehouse_id lateral edges
- Dashboard tasks in jobs referencing both dashboard_id and warehouse_id
- Other job task types (sql_task, dbt_task, notebook_task, alert_task, power_bi_task) referencing warehouse_id
- Quality monitors referencing warehouse_id
- Job pipeline_task referencing a DLT pipeline via pipeline_id (dagshund-247c)
- Serving endpoint referencing a registered_model that is absent from the plan (dagshund-1o0m)
- App with uc_securable reference — already present in app-dependencies fixture but ignored by code (dagshund-33dm)

---

## Session log

### Fixture #1: all-create — DONE (2026-04-14)

Reshape (landed earlier on main):
- Dropped dangling experiments.audit_analysis + registered_models.quality_metrics

Discovery: run_job_task had no lateral edge. Spun off as dagshund-aaby, landed in commit a86fd85.

Final review: considered adding a quality_monitor on analytics.curated_events to tighten narrative + cover phantom-table lateral edge, but the table wouldn't exist yet on a first deploy — QM creation would fail at apply time. Coverage for 3-part table_name QMs is already in lateral-deps (dagshund-6334, closed). Decision: leave all-create as-is, minor narrative snags accepted.

### Fixture #2: all-destroy — DONE

Comment cleanup only — no structural changes. Fixture correctly exercises every Dangerous Actions warning path (experiments, registered_models, schemas, volumes) via a broad resource set.
- before/ comment: dropped stale "Same resource set as all-create/after" claim, added decommissioning narrative + explanation of why it's intentionally broader
- after/ comment: added note that it pairs with before/ to exercise dangerous-action warnings

### Fixture #3: all-hierarchies — DONE (kept, de-emphasized)

Confirmed synthetic — hand-authored plan.json with no before/after YAML pair, exotic resource types (catalogs, database_*, postgres_*, synced_database_tables, external_locations) not reproducible in OSS workspace, cli_version drift (0.290.0 vs 0.296.0). Removes options for `just regen`.
- Kept fixture (Option C) — deleting it would break ~10 tests across 3 files that cover exotic resource type code paths
- Removed Pages index card
- Added README.md explaining synthetic nature, listing types it uniquely covers, warning against regen
- Filed dagshund-198b to replace with a real enterprise-workspace bundle

### Fixture #4: app-dependencies — DONE

Reshaped from identical before/after (no-op plan) to a **second deploy** story: the ETL pipeline has matured enough to plug in experiment tracking, a secret-backed external API call, and LLM inference.

before/: unchanged baseline — app with 3 refs (job, sql_warehouse, uc_securable), dangling experiment, jobs/my_etl_job.

after/: adds new model_serving_endpoints/app_chat_endpoint (bundle-owned, served from phantom_schema.phantom_model) and wires 3 new refs into the app:
- experiment_tracker (de-dangles my_experiment)
- api_token (phantom secret → CLI-managed `app_secrets` scope)
- chat_model (the new serving endpoint)

Plan shows: `+ model_serving_endpoints/app_chat_endpoint (create)`, `~ apps/my_test_app (update)`, `= experiments/my_experiment`, `= jobs/my_etl_job`.

#### Bugs surfaced and fixed inline

1. **experiment_id vs id mismatch** in `extractAppResourceReferences`: extractor read `experiment["id"]` but DAB emits `experiment["experiment_id"]` (per schema). Check never matched → no app→experiment lateral edge. Fix: read `experiment["experiment_id"]`. Updated 2 tests in extract-lateral-edges.test.ts that had stale fixture payloads.

2. **Phantom type badges missing in Dependencies panel**: `connected-nodes.ts` `toEntry` used `extractTypeBadge` for the "Depends on" / "Depended on by" lists, which only handles real resource keys (`resources.type.name`). Phantom IDs like `sql-warehouse::…`, `secret-scope::…`, `source-table::…` fell through. Fix: use `extractPhantomBadge` which handles both phantoms and falls through to extractTypeBadge for real resources. Warehouse/secret/table/experiment phantoms now show their (type) badge in the panel.

title: wheel-bump: convert to mixed classic+serverless fixture, regen ad hoc only
description:
The wheel-bump golden fixture is currently serverless-only because the default fixture workspace (Databricks Free Edition) is serverless-only and the Jobs API rejects task-level libraries there. The per-task tasks[task_key='X'].libraries[N].whl churn — the primary target of --suppress-wheel-updates — is therefore covered only by unit tests and the shared vectors (fixtures/wheel-update-cases.json), not by a golden fixture.

Plan:
1. Convert fixtures/golden/wheel-bump to MIXED compute: keep serverless environments (environment_key) on some tasks, and add job_clusters/new_cluster + task-level libraries[].whl on others. One fixture then exercises per-task wheel churn, per-environment wheel churn, and their combination. The pre-serverless cluster-based config exists in the git history of feature/wheel-skip; externals.yaml already has node_type_id for the cluster spec.
2. Regeneration requires a workspace where classic compute is available, so it happens ad hoc in a suitable environment — not part of the routine regen flow.
3. Exclude wheel-bump from automatic fixture regeneration: add it to the skip list in fixtures/tooling/regen.sh (same mechanism as the manual-drift interactive fixture, but with an 'ad hoc / needs classic compute' reason).
4. Document the exclusion and the ad-hoc procedure in BOTH the update-fixtures skill (skills/) AND fixtures/README.md (the 'just regen skips' table), plus anywhere else regen coverage is described, so nobody trips over it during routine CLI-version regens.
5. After regen: verify each classic task shows a libraries[N].whl update that --suppress-wheel-updates collapses into the per-job summary alongside the environment lines, then bless expected outputs (just gen-expected wheel-bump) and update the golden assertions in js/tests/graph/build-plan-graph.test.ts and tests/test_terminal.py that currently assume no wheel-only tasks.

Deferred review findings (3-pass review on feature/wheel-skip, 2026-07-03) — address together with the fixture conversion:
- TS: collectWheelUpdates classifies a task as wheel-only via isCountingChange only; a topology-drift re-add with action 'skip' on the same task would not disqualify it, so the browser could render a drifted task as unchanged under the toggle (drift pill on an unchanged-styled node). Fix: also treat isTopologyDriftChange entries as real changes in the else branch. Python is immune (drift lines always render). Likely unreachable today; verify against a real drift+wheel plan once classic churn exists.
- js/src/components/flow-canvas.tsx wheelUpdateCount comment + wheel-update-toggle.tsx JSDoc say 'distinct wheel updates across all jobs' but the value is a sum of per-job distinct bumps; reword.
- src/dagshund/cli.py --suppress-wheel-updates help says 'per-task' but the flag also covers serverless per-environment dependencies; broaden wording.
- README.md suppression paragraph has a comma splice ('...are suppressed, swapping...').

title: Unify selectedNode and selectedNodeId into single useState
description:
flow-canvas.tsx:45-46 — selectedNode (DagNodeData|null) and selectedNodeId (string|null) are always set/cleared in lockstep across 3 call sites (handleClosePanel, handlePaneClick, handleNodeClick). Could unify into useState<{ data: DagNodeData; id: string } | null> to eliminate structural drift risk.

Trade-off: saves one useState + one setter per mutation site, but adds destructuring at ~4 consumption sites. The two effectiveSelected* useMemo derivations would still be needed for the phantom-hidden check. Net value is marginal — the 3 mutation sites are all in the same file, so drift risk is low in practice.

Won't-fix for now. Revisit if flow-canvas state grows further or if selection logic moves to a hook.

title: recreate action should count as both add and delete in summary
description: The Databricks CLI counts 'recreate' in both 'to add' AND 'to delete' summary buckets. We currently count it as 'modified' only. Since recreate is destructive (deletes and recreates the resource), it should be flagged more prominently — at minimum counted correctly in the summary, possibly with a warning similar to stateful resource delete warnings.

title: Browser UI: handle all-skip plans and display 'unchanged' instead of 'skip'
description:
The browser visualization shows 'no plan' when given a plan where all resources have action 'skip' (e.g. fixtures/no-changes-plan.json). The JS pipeline likely filters out skip resources somewhere, leaving an empty graph.

## What needs investigating
1. Where in the JS parsing/graph pipeline are skip resources filtered out?
2. Does the app show 'no plan' because the graph ends up empty after filtering?

## What needs fixing
- All-skip plans should render meaningfully (e.g. show the DAG with all nodes styled as 'unchanged')
- The mapping layer (map-diff-state.ts) already maps skip → unchanged correctly
- The issue is likely in graph building or task extraction filtering out skip resources entirely

## Context
- Python text mode fix landed in dagshund-3ebj: skip → 'unchanged' labels, all-skip shows 'No changes (N resources unchanged)'
- Browser already has correct DiffState styling for 'unchanged' nodes
- Fixture: fixtures/no-changes-plan.json (8 resources, all action: skip)

description: text.py:193 calls sorted(resource_groups) but the dict keys are already in sorted order from _group_by_resource_type which sorts before groupby. Python 3.7+ dicts preserve insertion order. The sorted() is redundant. However it does make the ordering guarantee visible locally — consider adding a comment instead of removing it.

title: show synced-table managed outputs in Python renderers
description:
The Python terminal and Markdown renderers operate on raw plan resource entries and do not expose the additional resources materialized by synced-table bundle resources. A `postgres_synced_tables` entry is shown only once, so its generated pipeline and its Unity Catalog table output are invisible in Python output even though the bundle creates them. A `synced_database_tables` entry likewise materializes a Unity Catalog table and a PostgreSQL table, but the Python output does not communicate both effects.

Bring the Python output semantics in line with the managed-output model being added to the browser graph by dagshund-hw3o and dagshund-70w5.

Expected behavior:
- Show the managed pipeline and Unity Catalog table outputs of `postgres_synced_tables`, in addition to the owning PostgreSQL synced-table resource.
- Show both the Unity Catalog and PostgreSQL table effects of `synced_database_tables` rather than presenting the raw bundle entry as if it represented only one resource.
- Give generated outputs stable, human-readable type/name labels without pretending that they are independent raw plan entries.
- Inherit the owning resource's create, update, delete, or unchanged state, using new state and remote state appropriately.
- Keep action summaries and resource counts accurate and avoid accidental double-counting of the bundle operation; explicitly define whether managed outputs are included in summary counts.
- Ensure `--filter`, `--changes-only`, color/no-color output, Markdown output, and dangerous-action/manual-drift reporting remain coherent.
- Add focused Python tests plus golden terminal and Markdown coverage for create and delete cases, missing or malformed output fields, and both synced-table resource types.

The implementation should share managed-output extraction semantics across the Python renderers rather than adding renderer-specific special cases.
notes: Decision: render managed outputs as nested annotations on the owning resource. Exclude outputs from group/resource/action counts and warnings; filter owners and outputs as one unit; preserve the all-unchanged shortcut. Both postgres_synced_tables and synced_database_tables expose a synchronization pipeline. Treat explicit existing_pipeline_id as a reference rather than an owned output. For synced_database_tables, describe the PostgreSQL destination and its Unity Catalog registration as two surfaces of the same table, not two physical table copies. Update the real Lakebase create golden and cover delete/malformed/existing-pipeline/synced_database_tables cases with focused exact-output tests rather than a synthetic golden fixture.

title: fix: increase light mode --diff-added-soft alpha for better contrast
description: R3-MED-20. In light mode, --diff-added-soft: rgba(88,117,57,0.16) barely registers against --surface: #c8cad3. Added nodes don't stand out enough compared to the vivid red for removed. Fix: increase alpha on --diff-added-soft to at least 0.24 in light mode. Located in js/src/styles/index.css around lines 21-22. Compare against WCAG AA contrast requirements. title: Property-based tests for merge_sub_resources with Hypothesis
description:
src/dagshund/merge.py is the gnarliest logic in the repo (sub-resource absorption into parents, action promotion, state injection, self-referential dep filtering). Today it's covered by example tests + golden end-to-end fixtures. Property tests would prove invariants instead of just spot-checking them.

Add hypothesis to the dev dependency group. Invariants worth proving:

1. Orphan preservation — if a sub-resource key has no matching parent in the plan, merge_sub_resources preserves it verbatim under the original sub-resource key. (Already a code path in merge.py:180, worth a property not just an example.)

2. Idempotence on sub-free input — if the input has no sub-resource keys (no keys with >3 dot segments), merge_sub_resources(x) == x.

3. Action promotion rules in _promote_action:
   - parent='skip' or '', sub='update' => parent becomes 'update'
   - parent='delete', sub='update' => stays 'delete' (destructive wins)
   - parent='create', sub='create' => stays 'create'
   Generate action pairs, assert the promotion table.

4. depends_on sanity:
   - Self-referential edges (node == parent_key) never appear in merged output
   - Sub-resource-key targets are rewritten to their parent key

5. Field-key prefixing in _prefix_changes: for any sub with suffix S and field key K, the merged parent has a change at '{S}.{K}'. If the parent already has a field named '{S}.{K}' verbatim, document resolution order (current code: prefixed sub wins via dict spread order — is that intended?).

Each invariant is ~5 lines of @given. Not urgent — the code is stable and golden fixtures exercise it end-to-end. File under 'do when in a refactoring mood' or 'do alongside dagshund-161c to catch regressions during the typed-model refactor'.

Luxury, not priority. Skip if bored of the repo.

title: Refactor JavaScript plan preparation and graph architecture
description:
## Context
This epic tracks the JavaScript/TypeScript plan-preparation and resource-graph work identified by the earlier architecture review. All 11 existing children remain in scope. Current code already has centralized normalization logic/types, task-reference registries, derived-node conventions, and specialized resolvers; reuse these foundations rather than treating their capabilities as absent. The read-only audit reproduced stale-state/task behavior, reference deduplication errors, silent recognized-structure decoding failures, and real-versus-phantom identity discrepancies using constructed accepted inputs. Those are evidence of specific defects, not newly observed upstream Databricks incidents; each owning implementation must establish its own focused reproduction.

## Approved planning outcome
Prepare all 11 original children as bounded, implementation-ready tasks without replacing their IDs. Add the missing persistent review children and one explicit final integration record. Settle source-grounded technical details within the approved direction; return material behavior, architecture, interface, or scope conflicts for human decision rather than inventing requirements. Keep canonical task requirements in descriptions/acceptance_criteria and record only a concise plan index and approved decision deltas in parent notes/comments.

## Goal and approved direction
Establish one explicit data path from parsed input through normalization and narrow semantic preparation into graph construction.
- Normalize once near application orchestration, then prepare the resource/job/task semantics actually consumed by graph builders. Keep arbitrary Databricks resource state and unrelated fields opaque; retain original redacted input for its existing consumers.
- Use one current-state policy: present empty new state remains empty rather than restoring removed current fields, tasks, or relationships from remote state. Preserve appropriate remote-state rendering for deleted resources. Keep historical snapshots explicitly available for diffing and identity lookup; do not use that access as accidental current-state fallback.
- Surface safe resource/capability diagnostics for malformed recognized structures while retaining generic rendering where possible. Unknown types and unrelated fields remain accepted; do not replace envelope tolerance with full resource-schema validation.
- Share reference identity/resolution between phantom materialization and lateral-edge construction, including real, derived, and phantom identities. Deduplicate by resolved target. Preserve specialized behavior through existing registries or explicit exhaustive handling where semantics genuinely differ; do not invent a universal flag-heavy resolver.
- Correct the demonstrated stale-state, deduplication, and real-versus-phantom identity defects. Split graph-building responsibilities and update semantic contracts/documentation without redesigning unrelated UI.

## Scope
The existing children cover effective-state selection, resolved-reference deduplication, normalize-once ownership, safe semantic diagnostics, narrow job/task projections, shared reference descriptors and conventional/specialized migrations, responsibility-based graph module boundaries, semantic contract consolidation, and architecture documentation. Preserve all original implementation IDs. Coordinate overlapping contracts and stages so diagnostics/projections and reference migrations do not introduce competing implementations. Each implementation owns its initial characterization/regression tests; final contract consolidation must not defer foundational tests out of their owning changes.

## Non-goals and compatibility boundaries
No Python implementation changes, AI Gateway implementation, general CLI 1.20 feature expansion, complete Databricks schema model, exhaustive resource classes, plugin framework, new dependency, unrelated React/rendering or styling refactor, speculative safeguards, or file splitting solely for size/testability. Do not broaden intentionally unsupported reference shapes merely to make a generic abstraction appear complete. Preserve specialized edge directions, hierarchy/phantom placement and promotion, current filtering and detail semantics, source nonmutation, and opaque unknown resource support except for explicitly approved bug corrections. Shared fixtures must respect existing Python consumers; cross-language contracts apply only where semantics genuinely match and must not impose browser-specific fallback policies on Python safety analysis. No unreviewed mass golden update or fixture-family reorganization (dagshund-m1oo).

## Workflow, sequencing, and authority
Each child must reproduce or characterize its behavior before implementation. Tests belong to the owning change. Parent-child edges group work; only genuine explicit blocking edges impose implementation order. Preserve existing valid dependencies and this epic's blocker relationship to dagshund-n8zt unless the human explicitly revises sequencing. Prepare one persistent review child per implementation and one final integration child depending on the actual implementation IDs. Planning approval authorizes planner handoff and tracker preparation only, not builders, code changes, implementation worktrees, commits/integration, task closure, main merge, push, or publication. Execution requires a separate /implement preview and explicit approval.
acceptance_criteria:
- All 11 original implementation child IDs are retained and prepared in place with bounded outcomes, settled interfaces, exact change sites, regression cases, verification commands, and actual prerequisites. Add one persistent review child per implementation and one final integration child; keep only a concise parent index and decision deltas in notes/comments.
- Application orchestration normalizes once and graph consumers use prepared narrow semantics, while original redacted input and opaque unrelated resource state remain available without mutation.
- One current-state policy distinguishes present empty new state from absent new state. Empty objects/collections do not restore removed current fields, tasks, or references from remote state; deleted resources retain appropriate remote-state rendering. Historical diffing and identity lookup remain explicit rather than accidental fallback.
- Malformed recognized structures produce safe resource/capability diagnostics and generic rendering fallback where possible, rather than silently losing supported capabilities or rejecting unknown resource types/fields. Preparation and graph consumption do not independently decode the same structures.
- Phantom materialization and lateral edges share reference identity/resolution decisions, including real, derived, and phantom identities. Deduplication uses resolved targets. Preserve specialized semantics, supported relationships, and documented unsupported cases without a universal flag-heavy framework.
- Demonstrated stale-state/task, cross-kind deduplication, and real-versus-phantom identity bugs receive focused public-path regressions; other refactor behavior is preserved. Existing golden changes require an owning approved correction, not blanket reblessing.
- Graph-building responsibilities are separated along existing domain boundaries; internal interface changes serve the approved data path, not arbitrary file-size or testability goals. Existing registries and explicit exhaustive specialized behavior remain reusable sources of truth.
- Narrow semantic contracts and architecture documentation match implemented boundaries. Cross-language fixtures cover genuinely shared semantics without forcing Python safety analysis to adopt browser-specific fallback policies.
- Required tests, lint/type checks, golden checks, and affected browser behavior are verified through repository tooling. No Python implementation changes, AI Gateway work, general CLI 1.20 feature expansion, exhaustive schema, plugin framework, new dependency, or unrelated React/styling refactor is included.
- Planning approval authorizes only planner handoff and Beads preparation. Builders, implementation worktrees, code changes/commits, local integration, task closure, main merge, push, and publication require separately approved execution.

title: Implement: Centralize effective resource state selection
description:
## Outcome and boundaries
Centralize current snapshot selection before semantic preparation. This is the owning stale-state correction, not a schema or graph redesign. Follow .agents/guidelines/{TYPESCRIPT,VISUALIZATION,TESTING}.md. No prerequisites beyond execution approval.

## Source and policy
Change js/src/graph/extract-resource-state.ts (extractResourceState, extractStateField, extractExistingPipelineId) and js/src/graph/extract-tasks.ts (resolveTaskEntries, resolveJobState, resolveAllTaskEntries); migrate callers in build-plan-graph.ts, build-resource-graph.ts, collect-phantom-nodes.ts and extract-lateral-edges.ts. Current tests explicitly expect field/task fallback and must be replaced only for the approved correction.
Introduce one pure selector in js/src/utils/effective-resource-state.ts taking PlanEntry and returning the selected unknown snapshot plus its origin (new/remote/absent). For delete select remote_state. A malformed present wrapper is invalid selected new data, not a reason to use remote. Selection precedes record/projection validation. skip follows the same rule, with no special empty-array fallback. Undefined is absence; JSON null is present invalid data. Keep invalid data distinguishable for .4 diagnostics.
Within the selected record, omitted/non-string fields do not consult remote state. Top-level versus spec-nested aliases may still be tried within that same record. An empty job-level remainder may keep its existing undefined display convention, but must not restore remote job fields.

Owning additions include fixtures/effective-state-cases.json (.1), renderer-neutral normalization cases (.3), and preparation/reference vectors/tests (.4-.8). Inspect those exact integrated artifacts before adding overlapping files.

1. Build a concise matrix on this bead mapping semantic category -> fixture/cases -> actual JS test/entry point -> language applicability. 2. Fill concrete uncovered cases with small JSON inputs/expected semantic outputs and named consuming tests. Extend existing fixtures where semantics match; use adjacent narrow case files for genuinely JS-only behavior. Inputs are plan fragments or narrow projection inputs, not full Databricks schemas. Expected results use statuses, semantic IDs, target pairs or diff states, not React nodes, coordinates or CSS. Do not turn this into an exhaustive schema modeling exercise.
3. Preserve fixtures/job-run-effect-cases.json expected.phantomId compatibility: Python legitimately keeps some orphan effects standalone while JS adapts semantic orphan targets into graph phantoms. JS normalization tests can translate that legacy expectation without changing Python behavior. Do not force Python safety analysis to adopt browser current-state policy. No related/discovered-from Python bead is created unless the human explicitly approves adoption; record a candidate gap here for coordinator decision instead.
4. Keep owning public-path regressions and full graph goldens. Consolidate only truly duplicate semantic cases, preserving failure coverage and provenance. Do not reorganize fixture families (dagshund-m1oo), hand-edit generated goldens or rebless unexplained output.

Perform the entire behavior-preserving decomposition of js/src/graph/resolve-references.ts as ONE cohesive implementation. User execution approval is dagshund-yy49 comment470. This replaces the five-stage draft; do not execute the superseded sibling stages or introduce temporary APIs to support them. Read parent dagshund-yy49.14 requirements as the scope boundary. ## Concrete ownership boundaries
- graph/build-reference-identity-catalog.ts owns buildReferenceIdentityCatalog and private hierarchy identity/node-ID helpers. Preserve its current public signature, all seven maps, ordered passes and last-entry precedence. Branch identities precede symbolic database lookup; final pipeline index overrides must remove stale real-resource aliases for derived targets. Keep ReferenceIdentityCatalog and ReferenceResolution in types/reference-resolution.ts unchanged.
- graph/reference-resolution-context.ts is a readonly type-only context owner. Domain modules import it directly, not through the orchestrator. Do not retain finalRunJobTargets on shared context: the coordinator computes the existing buildFinalRunJobTargets once and passes the map explicitly to task resolution.
- graph/resolve-conventional-references.ts owns resolveConventionalReference, preserving conventional registry extraction and absent/unsupported markers.
- graph/resolve-task-references.ts owns prepared task and run-job relationships. Export resolvePreparedTaskReferences(sourceResourceKey, context, finalRunJobTargets); private helpers reuse TASK_REF_SPECS and existing resolve-run-job-target.ts decisions. Never decode tasks or clusters again.
- graph/resolve-workspace-references.ts owns instance-pool and Vector Search endpoint relationships. Retain real-only behavior, exact supported interpolations and selected-state name lookup.
- graph/resolve-postgres-references.ts owns catalog/database, branch-lineage and database-role relationships. Use named private domain branches and prepared Postgres fields; reuse postgres-paths.ts and catalog maps. Preserve branch-before-parent resolution priority, normalized identity before exact branch-ref/database fallback, allowed hierarchy phantoms and real-only role behavior.
- graph/resolve-lakebase-references.ts owns database-instance and existing-pipeline relationships. Existing-pipeline lookup consumes only prepared existingPipelineId for both synced-table families; preserve supported/absent/unsupported ownership authority and index/symbolic/fallback priorities. Keep its tiny shared descriptor constructor private, not a general factory layer.
- graph/resolve-uc-table-references.ts owns source-table dependency decisions and exports findPromotedSourceTable for app reuse. Preserve derived-kind priority before owner order; source-specific self/owned-output suppression must not leak into apps. Reuse existing owned derived references and registry conventions.
- graph/resolve-pipeline-references.ts owns ingestion schema eligibility and its private evidence collection. Real schema targets always resolve; missing schemas require the same independent table/UC/serving/app evidence as today. Ingestion alone must not invent hierarchy evidence.
- graph/derived-node-specs.ts additionally owns a small resolveDerivedOutputReferences(sourceResourceKey, ownedDerivedRefs) consumer returning the existing output-to-owner descriptors. It must not rediscover ownership or alter preparation.
- graph/resolve-app-references.ts owns the exhaustive app resource switch and its private named-target helper. Preserve each resource family's index/key/symbolic/phantom policies and shared UC promotion helper.
- graph/resolve-serving-references.ts owns serving-model references. Preserve full-name index -> registered-model resource key -> selected full_name scan -> selected name scan; only unresolved qualified names create hierarchy phantoms.

## Final orchestration and callers
resolve-references.ts computes the existing final run-job map once from jobs and composes, per entry, in the existing sequence: conventional single result; Postgres; source table; derived ownership; pipeline ingestion; serving model; app; prepared tasks; database instance; existing pipeline; instance pools; vector endpoint. title: Implement: Deduplicate task references by resolved target
description:
## Outcome
Fix the narrow cross-kind deduplication defect in js/src/graph/extract-lateral-edges.ts:createJobTaskRefsSpec. It currently adds raw IDs to one seen set before calling resolveTaskRefTargetKey, so a warehouse can suppress a dashboard or pipeline with the same ID. No prerequisites; this fix must be retained by later descriptor migration .7. Follow TypeScript, visualization and testing guidelines.

## Steps
1. Reproduce through parsePlanJson -> buildResourceGraph with one job containing warehouse/dashboard/pipeline task references that use the same string. Assert target node IDs and exact lateral source/target pairs, not only counts. Cover phantom targets and matching real resources.
2. In createJobTaskRefsSpec, extract ID, resolve target key using TASK_REF_SPECS and resolveTaskRefTargetKey, translate to final node ID through resolveExistingTargetId, then deduplicate successful final target IDs. Do not mark raw IDs seen. Existing applyLateralEdgeSpec pair deduplication is compatible; avoid adding a competing resolver.
3. Cover multiple task refs and symbolic/API-ID aliases that reach one target; preserve the existing derived pipeline index path and absent-target behavior. Keep this implementation small. Reference identity/support-policy fixes belong to .7/.8, not here.

## Tests and verification
Add regressions to js/tests/graph/extract-lateral-edges.test.ts and js/tests/graph/build-resource-graph.test.ts. Reuse existing build graph helpers and supported TASK_REF_SPECS shapes; do not modify production exports for tests.
nix develop --command bun test --cwd js tests/graph/extract-lateral-edges.test.ts tests/graph/build-resource-graph.test.ts tests/graph/collect-phantom-nodes.test.ts
nix develop --command just typecheck-js
nix develop --command bun run --cwd js biome check src/ tests/
No generated fixture change is expected; any discovered delta needs owning regression evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- A parsed job with warehouse, dashboard and pipeline references sharing the same raw string yields all three distinct lateral targets, for both real-target and phantom-target cases.
- Repeated task refs and symbolic/API-ID aliases resolving to one final target yield one lateral edge per source/target, including derived pipeline aliases where supported.
- A failed/unavailable resolution does not suppress a later valid different-kind reference with the same raw value.
- Phantom IDs, labels, placement, task visibility and unrelated edge directions remain unchanged; inputs are unchanged.
- Focused public resource-graph and lateral-edge regressions, typecheck and nonmutating lint pass.

title: Implement: Make normalized plans a first-class boundary
description:
## Outcome and source
Expose the already-existing NormalizedPlan boundary, rather than inventing another normalizer. Entry points: js/src/app.tsx:PlanView/countByTab/DagView; js/src/utils/normalize-plan.ts:NormalizedEntry/NormalizedPlan/normalizePlan; graph/build-plan-graph.ts and build-resource-graph.ts; hooks/use-plan-graph.ts and use-resource-graph.ts; components/resources-view.tsx; js/scripts/extract-graph.ts:main. No prerequisite on the state correction. Follow TypeScript, visualization and testing guidelines.

## Contract and steps
1. Characterize mixed/sub-resource/job-run/no-changes plans and empty/orphan-only plans before refactoring. Keep normalizePlan(rawEntries) as the pure normalization entry. NormalizedPlan retains entries and attached effects. It does not contain React or phantom rendering decisions.
2. Change orphanEffects from a map keyed by job::<id> to readonly semantic orphan groups: each has targetResourceType: 'jobs', targetId: number and effects: readonly JobRunEffect[]. Preserve deterministic effect name ordering and grouping by semantic target. Remove phantomKind from EFFECT_TYPE_SPECS; graph/collect-phantom-nodes.ts:buildOrphanEffectPhantoms owns adaptation with buildPrefixedNodeId('job', String(targetId)). Preserve unresolved effects with no numeric target as standalone entries and effects-first node collision behavior.
3. Memoize normalizePlan(plan.plan ?? {}) once in PlanView. countByTab accepts NormalizedPlan. Pass the normalized result to DagView, ResourcesView, hooks and both builders. Keep PlanContext.Provider value={plan} unchanged for utils/extract-raw-plan-entry.ts and raw-json-disclosure consumers. Do not move normalization into each hook or make normalization effectful. .4 deliberately evolves graph consumers from NormalizedPlan to PreparedPlan; that is the next stage, not an overload needed here.
4. Update extract-graph.ts to normalize once after parsing. Update test call sites explicitly, retaining tests of parser -> normalize -> graph composition. Reuse helpers in js/tests/helpers only if they express that public path without changing fixture loading semantics for other consumers.
5. Adapt js/tests/utils/normalize-plan.test.ts to assert semantic orphan target groups while keeping fixtures/job-run-effect-cases.json expected.phantomId usable by existing Python tests. Map that expectation to the graph adapter in JS; do not rewrite its existing schema for a JS-only internal representation. Add renderer-neutral normalization cases separately where needed, including nonmutation and sub-resource/effect ordering, for .10 to consolidate later.

## Verification
Tests: js/tests/utils/{normalize-plan,merge-sub-resources,job-run-effects,extract-raw-plan-entry}.test.ts; js/tests/graph/{build-plan-graph,build-resource-graph,job-runs-fixture,collect-phantom-nodes}.test.ts; add js/tests/app.test.tsx for shared orchestration/count and original-context behavior using existing happy-dom/testing-library setup, no new dependencies.
nix develop --command just test-js
nix develop --command just typecheck-js
nix develop --command bun run --cwd js biome check src/ tests/
nix develop --command just test-golden
No expected graph behavior change is authorized in this boundary refactor.
acceptance_criteria:
- PlanView computes one memoized NormalizedPlan per parsed plan; countByTab, both graph hooks and both graph builders consume that same result without calling normalizePlan themselves.
- js/scripts/extract-graph.ts normalizes once and reuses the result for both builders; all callers/tests use the explicit boundary with no raw-Plan compatibility overload that hides normalization.
- PlanContext still supplies the original parsed/redacted pre-merge Plan for raw details; sub-resource changes, effect annotations and input objects are not mutated.
- Orphan effects carry semantic target type/ID and effects, not phantom-prefixed map keys; browser adaptation preserves job::<id>, effects-first deduplication, labels and tab behavior.
- Existing effect attachment/outcome vectors remain compatible with Python consumers; normalization/orphan contracts and browser graph regressions land here.
- JS tests, typecheck, nonmutating lint and golden checks pass without unexplained behavior drift.

title: Implement: Surface semantic preparation diagnostics
description:
## Outcome and prerequisites
After .3 (normalized boundary) and .1 (effective state), establish the narrow preparation/result boundary and its browser diagnostic consumer. Initial end-to-end capability is **serving endpoint model references**, currently js/src/graph/extract-resource-state.ts:extractServedEntities, graph/extract-lateral-edges.ts:createServingEndpointModelSpec and graph/build-resource-graph.ts:collectServingEndpointModelIdentities. This choice avoids owning job/task decoding (.5) or changing reference resolution (.6-.8). Follow TypeScript, visualization and testing guidelines.

## Settled interfaces
Add js/src/types/prepared-plan.ts and js/src/preparation/prepare-plan.ts. A readonly Projection<T> is {status:'absent'} | {status:'supported', value:T} | {status:'unsupported', diagnostic:PreparationDiagnostic}. Diagnostic fields are resourceKey, capability (stable code), and reason (static code, initially invalid-shape); user text is selected from static labels. No raw values or Zod errors enter this model.
PreparedPlan contains normalized: NormalizedPlan, byResourceKey: ReadonlyMap<string, PreparedResource>, diagnostics: readonly PreparationDiagnostic[]. PreparedResource initially contains currentState: Projection<Readonly<Record<string,unknown>>> and servedEntityNames: Projection<readonly string[]>; later beads extend only the capabilities they consume. Unknown resource types still receive the generic current record and absent specialized capabilities. Original entry/snapshots remain in normalized.entries, not copied into a new full resource schema.
preparePlan selects via .1 then validates only the record boundary and consumed slices with readonly Zod schemas. An absent snapshot is absent; malformed selected data is unsupported and cannot restore remote data. Aggregate each resource/capability diagnostic once. Normal valid absent capabilities are not warnings.

## Ordered steps
1. Characterize current silent served_entities failure through parsed plan -> resource graph; add js/tests/preparation/prepare-plan.test.ts covering valid new and remote endpoint_details shapes, missing, [], non-array, invalid containers and unknown fields. Unknown entity fields/types (e.g. external-model data) stay opaque; an entity_name field is validated as string only when present, and entries without it add no model reference. Preserve existing within-selected-snapshot precedence between config and endpoint_details, with malformed present recognized data reported rather than silently replaced.
2. Implement preparePlan and the serving projection in js/src/preparation/prepare-serving-endpoint.ts. Migrate both listed graph consumers to the same prepared names, preserving current real-model/phantom lookup behavior. Generic endpoint nodes still render on unsupported capability. Remove orphaned duplicate served-entity decoder only once its callers are migrated.
3. In app.tsx:PlanView, memoize preparePlan(normalizedPlan). Both graph builders/hooks and ResourcesView/DagView accept PreparedPlan, accessing normalized data explicitly. countByTab continues consuming normalized entries. Update js/scripts/extract-graph.ts and test composition to normalize once, prepare once, build both graphs. No hidden per-builder preparation wrapper.
4. Add components/preparation-diagnostics.tsx: a nonblocking details/summary warning count plus a list of resource keys and static capability messages above tab content. Render strings through React text, never HTML. Keep graphs usable, ready state intact, existing detail UI unchanged. Tests in js/tests/components/preparation-diagnostics.test.tsx and app.test.tsx use existing testing-library setup. Include sentinel secret values in invalid state and assert they are absent from diagnostic objects and rendered text.

## Verification
nix develop --command just test-js
nix develop --command just typecheck-js
nix develop --command bun run --cwd js biome check src/ tests/
nix develop --command just test-golden
Manually inspect warning disclosure and both tabs for a malformed serving endpoint plus a valid unknown resource. No new dependency, full resource schema, reference-policy change, Python implementation or unrelated styling work.
acceptance_criteria:
- preparePlan(NormalizedPlan) is pure and returns a PreparedPlan with resource-keyed narrow results and safe diagnostics; PlanView prepares once and both graph hooks/builders reuse it. Original redacted PlanContext remains unchanged.
- Results distinguish absent, supported (including empty arrays), and unsupported recognized capability data. Only invalid envelope parsing rejects the plan; semantic failures keep generic resource rendering.
- Initial serving-endpoint model projection reads selected config.served_entities or endpoint_details.config.served_entities once; graph phantom collection and lateral edges consume the same prepared names without re-decoding.
- Malformed selected resource records/recognized serving structures yield resource/capability diagnostics; unknown resource types, opaque extra fields and absent model-name fields remain tolerated.
- The nonblocking warning disclosure is testable and accessible; static messages expose no raw state, offending values, Zod messages, arbitrary paths or secrets.
- Focused preparation/DOM/public graph happy and failure tests, full JS tests, typecheck/lint and golden checks pass.
